title: EGCG@ZIF-8@Polydopamine-Functionalized Janus Nanofibrous Dressing with Directional Exudate Transport and Photothermal Antibacterial Activity for Infected Wound Treatment
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The treatment of infected skin wounds continues to face multiple challenges, including bacterial resistance, persistent inflammation, oxidative damage, and inadequate exudate management. To address these issues, a multifunctional Janus wound dressing was constructed to achieve coordinated infection control and tissue repair. Zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) was used as a nanocarrier for the natural antioxidant molecule, and polydopamine surface coating endowed the composite nanoparticles with photothermal antibacterial activity. The composite nanoparticles were subsequently incorporated into a hydrophobic polycaprolactone layer by electrospinning and combined with a hydrophilic polyacrylonitrile layer containing a pH indicator, thereby forming a bilayer structure with unidirectional liquid transport, visual monitoring, and wound protection functions. The dressing promotes the outward transfer of wound exudate and produces an observable color response to changes in environmental pH. Under near-infrared irradiation, the antibacterial rate of the dressing reached 98.89% against E. coli and 99.99% against S. aureus. The dressing also possesses excellent free-radical-scavenging capacity, indicating its potential to alleviate excessive oxidative stress in infected wounds. Animal experiments further demonstrated that the dressing reduced the local infection burden, promoted wound closure, collagen deposition, and tissue formation, and caused no obvious histopathological abnormalities in major organs. Overall, this study presents a multifunctional Janus nanofibrous dressing that integrates antibacterial activity, antioxidant function, exudate regulation, and wound-status monitoring, providing a material-design approach for the repair of infected skin wounds.

title: Synergetic Nano-bending, Photo-switching, and Macrocycle Shuttling Effects of Vibration-Induced Emission Lassos on Photoluminescence Properties of Hydrazone-Based [1]Rotaxanes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract 9,14-Diphenyl-9,14-dihydrodibenzo[a,c]phenazine (DPAC) fluorophores exhibited large Stokes shifts and vibration-induced emission (VIE) with bistable cyan (at 475 nm) and orange (at 600 nm) emissions, whereas hydrazone fluorophores (cyan emission at 475 nm) underwent reversible Z/E photo-isomerization, enabling efficient photo-switching. Herein, we introduced synergetic nano-bending and photo-switchable effects on optical switchable hydrazone linkers and macrocycle shuttling effects of VIE-active DPAC stoppers in [1]rotaxanes, wherein mechanically interlocked architecture-imposed spatial constraints could modulate photoluminescence (PL) behaviors in response to multiple external stimuli. Surprisingly, the highest lifetime τavg1 = 11.8 ns (cyan emission lifetime monitored at 475 nm) was obtained in the loosened lasso owing to stronger intramolecular hydrogen bonds of hydrazone units with minor constraints of nano-bending. While macrocycle shuttling was acid/base-triggered between the loosened lasso with a near-white-light emission [CIE (0.26, 0.32)] and the tightened lasso with an orange emission [CIE (0.37, 0.36)], [1]rotaxanes could tune synergetic PL emissions by modulating bent/planar conformations of DPAC units via acid/base controls and Z/E photo-isomerization of hydrazone units upon 365/450 nm exposures in isopropanol (IPA), respectively. The non-interlocked analogue exhibited the largest lifetime decrease (Δτavg1 = –1.9 ns), whereas the loosened and tightened lassos showed smaller decreases of Δτavg1 = –1.6 and –0.6 ns, respectively, demonstrating that nano-bending constraints suppressed hydrogen-bond disruption during Z/E photo-isomerization. Furthermore, the loosened lasso exhibited temperature- and viscosity-responsive emissions due to hydrogen-bonding disruptions of hydrazone units and progressive planarization of DPAC units upon heating to induce lower viscosity. These results highlight the potential of [1]rotaxanes as stimuli-responsive luminescent molecular systems, enabling proof-of-concept demonstrations in temperature and viscosity sensing as well as optical information encoding.

title: Polar crystals as catalytic platforms for solar energy conversion
abstract: Polar crystals possess non-centrosymmetric structures that generate spontaneous polarization and a built-in electric field, enabling efficient charge separation. This Review discusses their use as catalysts for converting solar energy into chemical energy, covering the advantages of polar single crystals, multilevel polarization engineering, key challenges and future directions.

title: Pain-Perception-Inspired Neuromorphic Sensing: Nonmonotonic Electrical Response and Spatial Visualization in a Near-Infrared-Responsive MXene Hydrogel
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic sensory devices that encode environmental stimuli at the sensing interface offer a route toward more adaptive machine–environment interactions. Ionic hydrogels provide mechanically compliant, ion-conducting hydrated networks that can incorporate photothermal components. However, many near-infrared (NIR)-responsive hydrogels show conductivity changes in one direction, while terminal electrical signals provide little information about stimulus location. Achieving response-direction reversal and spatially resolved visual feedback in one soft material using a single NIR input, therefore, remains challenging. Inspired by protective inhibition and post-stimulus rebound in pain-related neural signaling, we developed an NIR neuromorphic sensory device based on a Ca–PAA–EMB@IL-MXene hydrogel. The material couples photothermal conversion by IL-MXene with temperature-dependent ion transport in a hydrated Ca2+-coordinated PAA-EMB network. Weak irradiation transiently enhances conductivity, whereas stronger or prolonged irradiation drives the conductivity through a maximum into a suppressed state, followed by rebound and recovery after stimulus removal. Thermal, electrical, optical, and water-state measurements are consistent with heat-induced water redistribution and reorganization of the hydrated network, with the characteristic transition temperatures regulated by the EMB content. Programmed NIR pulses further produce paired-pulse facilitation-like behavior, signal accumulation, and responses dependent on recent stimulation history. Localized irradiation induces reversible whitening in the exposed region, supplementing the overall electrical signal with spatial information. An impedance-acquisition and microcontroller interface converts these responses into initial, strong-stimulus warning, and recovery states. This work provides a soft-material strategy for encoding NIR stimulus intensity, duration, history, and location through coupled electrical and optical outputs, supporting NIR-responsive neuromorphic sensing and warning interfaces.

title: Quantifying Anion Selectivity in SEI Formation for Ether-Based Electrolytes in Lithium Metal Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract While current electrolyte design strategies for lithium metal batteries (LMBs) emphasize the importance of an anion-dominated Li+ solvation structure to promote an inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), solvation structure-SEI composition relationships remain challenging to quantify. Here, we systematically investigate a series of ether/lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl) imide (LiFSI) electrolytes and quantify the lithium fluoride formed from FSI– decomposition using nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy. We find that both an anion-dominated electrolyte solvation structure and a reductively stable solvent are necessary to achieve anion-selective SEI formation and establish a framework for anion selectivity in ether-LiFSI electrolytes, guided by density functional theory-derived solvent descriptors, which aligns with existing examples of ether-based Li metal electrolytes. Using this model, we identify an electrolyte formulation of tert-butyl methyl ether and tert-amyl methyl ether that achieves a Coulombic efficiency of 99.3%. Ultimately, this study establishes key electrolyte solvent-interphase-performance relationships to enable high-performance LMBs.

title: Heterophase-Engineered Cs3Cu2I5/CsCu2I3 Memristors with Two-Step Resistive Switching
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The quest for energy-efficient memory technologies is critically hindered by the performance gap between high-performing but toxic lead-based perovskites and their environmentally benign yet less reliable lead-free counterparts. Here, we address this challenge by engineering the controlled coexistence of crystallographically 0D Cs3Cu2I5 and 1D CsCu2I3 phases using a scalable, hot-air-assisted process. The resulting heterophase architecture produces composition-dependent structural, interfacial, and chemical environments that strongly influence resistive-switching behavior. The optimized devices exhibit a high ON/OFF ratio of up to 7.4 × 108, more than three orders of magnitude higher than that of the corresponding single-phase films, together with electroforming-free operation and a reproducible two-step SET process that provides distinct resistance states for multilevel memory operation. Combined electrical, XPS, cross-sectional STEM/EDS, and post-switching ToF-SIMS analyses support a hybrid valence-change memory/electrochemical metallization (VCM-ECM) filament-evolution framework involving halide-deficient pathways, Cu–O-related oxygen-containing environments, and redistribution of Ag- and Cu-containing species. The two-step SET behavior and two threshold-like regions in the log–log I–V characteristics are consistent with multistage changes in trap occupancy and conductive-path connectivity without requiring direct assignment of the individual transitions to specific vacancy species. These results demonstrate heterophase engineering as an effective materials strategy for regulating local ionic and electronic transport in lead-free halide memristors and provide a pathway toward high-performance, multilevel nonvolatile memory and other ionically active solid-state devices.

title: Spatially Programmed Water Access Reconciles Service Stability with Triggered Post-Use Degradation in Biobased Multilayer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Sustainable packaging plastics often face a fundamental paradox: the material must resist moisture and remain stable during service, yet undergo controlled disassembly after disposal. Therefore, sustainable materials should not be evaluated solely based on their service performance or degradation rate, but rather on their ability to undergo effective functional transitions at critical stages throughout the lifecycle. Here, we developed a spatially programmed design strategy that addresses these conflicting requirements by regulating not only when and where water enters the material, but also how the degradation proceeds. The film consists of a hydrophilic, pectin-based inner layer, a hydrophobic polylactic acid (PLA) outer layer, and a hydrogen-bonded interface formed via hydrogen bonding. During packaging service, the PLA layer acts as a moisture-shielding skin, maintaining wet stability, barrier performance, and mechanical integrity. A key conceptual advance of this work lies in turning an inherent weakness into a lifecycle-regulating function, where water sensitivity serves as a trigger rather than a limitation. After use, assisted by mechanical damage, water activates the pectin/deep eutectic solvent (DES) phase. The acidic, water-rich microenvironment generated by the pectin/DES supports preferential cleavage near the PLA chain ends, promoting progressive molecular weight reduction while preventing premature failure that could compromise service performance. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further establish a molecular-level structure–function relationship within the architecture. The calculated interfacial binding energies and molecular interactions elucidate the origin of structural stability during service, while comparative analysis of PLA ester bond cleavage pathways demonstrates a more favorable energetic pathway for terminal ester cleavage after activation, supporting the chain-end-preferential degradation tendency. In contrast to conventional multilayer materials that mainly improve individual properties, this work provides insights into biopolymer design, moving beyond the long-standing trade-off paradigm of stability and degradability by spatially programming these functions as complementary components within a lifecycle-balanced architecture.

title: Co-generation of energy and data for hyperscale data center based on distributionally robust CVaR framework
abstract: The proliferation of hyperscale data centers (DCs) has imposed unprecedented strain on local grid capacity, threatening power system stability and decarbonization targets. To confront these challenges, this paper proposes a co-generation framework for energy and data that jointly optimizes on-site generation planning and computational workload scheduling via a bilevel stochastic program under a distributionally robust CVaR (DR-CVaR) framework. In the upper level, the DC operator minimizes the annualized life-cycle cost under stressed operating conditions by co-optimizing the capacity of hydrogen-ready gas turbines (HRGT), small modular reactors (SMR), renewables, and battery energy storage systems (BESS), alongside spatio-temporal workload allocation across DC sites. In the lower level, the transmission system operator clears the day-ahead market via DC optimal power flow, returning locational marginal prices that couple the DC's planning and operation decisions with wholesale market incentives; the bilevel model is reformulated through the lower-level optimality conditions and strong duality, and the reported plans are computed by a two-stage procedure whose distance from the bilevel optimum is bounded by 1.3% in the headline configurations. Case studies on the IEEE RTS-24 bus system cover 100 MW brownfield and 1000 MW greenfield deployments in a stress-test planning setting under extreme-event scenarios. At the 100 MW scale, relative to an inelastic-load baseline, computational flexibility alone reduces expected total cost by 3.19%, and the full framework reduces grid risk adder costs by 29.36%. At the 1000 MW scale, on-site generation becomes a feasibility precondition rather than a cost refinement: hourly 24/7 carbon-free energy (CFE) matching substitutes firm clean capacity for fuel and grid procurement, reducing operating costs by 9.29% relative to daily volumetric accounting at a 1.06% higher total cost. Sensitivity analysis further shows that complete energy self-sufficiency is achievable at full clean self-supply (ψ=1.0) through 100% SMR provision, at a 25.12% total cost premium. These results provide economic and technical guidance for future DC deployment.

title: The surprising reason women in academia do more parenting than men
abstract: Policies designed to keep women in the workforce could be entrenching gendered parenting roles.

title: Entangled-to-packed crossover in nonlinear extensional rheology of entangled polymers
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The tube model, which reduces the interaction of many-chain entanglement to a single-chain picture, has enabled quantitative descriptions of the mechanical behaviors of polymeric materials and underpins applications from polymer processing to life sciences. In strong extensional flows, however, this theory systematically fails. Herein, through molecular dynamics simulations of entangled polymers, we reveal a strain-induced crossover from the entangled state to a packed state in the inter-chain configuration. Following the saturation of primitive chain stretch, convective disentanglement and chain alignment reorganize the system into a packed configuration of aligned segments. This crossover makes an explicit inter-chain contribution necessary for describing tensile stress beyond the intra-chain conformational stress, explaining the breakdown of tube-based descriptions and quantitatively capturing the mechanical response at large extensional strains. These findings clearly show how the inter-chain reorganization governs the nonlinear extensional behaviors.

title: Molecular-level control of nitrogen sites enables CO2 electro-reduction under industrially relevant conditions
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Industrial flue gases typically contain only 3–15% CO2, and direct electrochemical reduction on such dilute feeds would eliminate costly upstream purification. However, mass transport limitations and competing hydrogen evolution severely restrict activity under these CO2-starved conditions, and the governing molecular factors remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that pyridinic-nitrogen enrichment in Ni–N–C single-atom catalysts enables efficient CO2 reduction under dilute CO2. By tuning the pyridinic-N to pyrrolic-N ratio in well-defined Ni–Nx sites, we probe the role of local nitrogen environments in CO2 reduction rather than the metal center alone. Electronic-state analysis and density functional theory reveal that pyridinic-N forms a reversible CO2 adduct that enhances local CO2 accessibility near the active Ni center through a desorption–re-adsorption relay. These findings provide molecular-level insight by identifying a neighboring motif that regulates local CO2 availability without perturbing the intrinsic Ni–N reaction pathway, and by establishing a transferable design principle for CO2 reduction catalysts under CO2-limited conditions.

title: Engineering phosphorescence and pH-responsive fluorescence of molecular luminophores and elastomers
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Organic ultralong room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) enables time-gated optical readout by separating long-lived triplet emission from short-lived autofluorescence. However, coupling RTP with biochemical responsiveness at both the molecular and materials levels remains a fundamental challenge due to the lack of a luminophore-intrinsic design principle for linking chemical responsiveness to triplet-state photophysics and the conflict between rigid, shielded microenvironments and deformable polymer matrices. Here we present an ArKMK design paradigm that electronically couples an aromatic ketone to a pH-responsive α-methyleneketone within a carbonyl-rich framework, yielding homophthalic anhydride (HA) and homophthalimides as a family of luminophores that integrate pH responsiveness with RTP. To preserve long-lived emission in elastomeric matrices, we further develop a two-pots-in-one (TPiO) strategy that separately preforms hydrophilic and hydrophobic segments and then co-reacts them to generate phase-separated microenvironments in biodegradable polyesters. The resulting materials reconcile mechanical compliance with triplet-state stabilization, while covalently integrating ArKMK luminophores through the same esterification chemistry. These biodegradable polyesters enable time-gated subcutaneous imaging, gastrointestinal tracking and wound-status reporting through coupled RTP and pH-indicating fluorescence. This work establishes a molecular-to-polymer framework for integrating pH responsiveness with long-lived triplet emission in soft, biodegradable materials.

title: Strong hydrogels through precisely oriented crystallization regulation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Achieving high mechanical strength and environmental stability is critical for hydrogels in demanding engineering scenarios. Crystalline hydrogels hold promise because their crystallites act as physical crosslinks and energy dissipators; however, precise control over crystalline architecture remains underexplored. Inspired by industrial thermoplastic processing, we report an ASGS strategy for crystalline hydrogels that integrates alkali-induced chain activation (A), ultra-stretching-driven orientation (S), and glycerol-seawater-mediated densification (GS). Alkali treatment yields moderate initial crystallinity with refined nascent crystallites. Ultra-stretching establishes a highly oriented chain network, and subsequent densification achieves maximum crystallinity and highly oriented crystallites. The resultant hydrogels, in the fully hydrated state, combine a tensile strength of 160.0 MPa, a modulus of 746.0 MPa, and a fracture energy of 26.4 kJ·m⁻². The corresponding plastic reaches 414.2 MPa tensile strength while retaining flexibility. This thermoplastic-inspired crystallization engineering provides a scalable paradigm for fabricating strong and stable crystalline hydrogels, promising for load-bearing and harsh underwater engineering applications.

title: Coordination-directed synthesis of two-dimensional metal-organic covalent organic frameworks
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Metal-organic covalent organic frameworks (MOCOFs) combine the advantages of covalent and metal-organic frameworks, but research remains sparse due to characterization difficulties, leaving unclear whether their formation is covalent- or coordination-directed. To date, only a few three-dimensional MOCOFs have been reported, while two-dimensional (2D) MOCOFs remain unexplored. Here, we strategically synthesize two single-crystal 2D MOCOFs with high porosity, denoted as PUMC-1 and PUMC-2. Leveraging three-dimensional electron diffraction, we are able to elucidate their formation process in detail. First, one-dimensional coordination polymers (1D CPs) are constructed from two sub-building units: tetrakis(4-aminophenyl) porphyrin and cobalt(II) trans-A₂B₂ porphyrin. Second, 1D CPs with covalent extension sites are used to construct two distinct 2D MOCOF conformations via covalent self-assembly under different conditions. Notably, the same 2D MOCOFs can also be directly obtained via one-pot synthesis with the same monomers, providing experimental evidence for a coordination-directed covalent assembly mechanism. This work not only expands the dimensionality of MOCOFs but also opens new avenues in reticular chemistry.

title: Conveyor-mode electron shuttling through a T-junction in Si/SiGe
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Conveyor-mode shuttling in gated Si/SiGe devices enables adiabatic transfer of single electrons, electron patterns and spin qubits confined in quantum dots across several microns with a scalable number of signal lines. To realize their full potential, linear shuttle lanes must connect into a two-dimensional grid with controllable routing. We introduce a T-junction device linking two independently driven shuttle lanes. Electron routing across the junction requires no extra control lines beyond the four channels per conveyor belt. We measure an inter-lane charge transfer fidelity of F={100.0000000}_{-9\times 1{0}^{-7}}^{+0}\,\% at an instantaneous electron velocity of 270 mm s−1. The filling of 54 quantum dots is controlled by simple atomic pulses, allowing us to swap electron patterns, laying the groundwork for a native spin-qubit SWAP gate. This T-junction establishes a path towards scalable, two-dimensional quantum computing architectures with flexible spin qubit routing for quantum error correction.

title: Strong-gain water-window X-ray laser driven by plasma photocathode wakefield acceleration
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: X-ray free-electron lasers are large and complex machines, limited by electron beam brightness. Here we show through start-to-end simulations how to realise compact, robust and tunable X-ray lasers in the water window, based on ultra-bright electron beams from plasma wakefield accelerators. First, an ultra-low-emittance electron beam is released by a plasma photocathode in a metre-scale plasma wakefield accelerator. By tuning the beam charge, space-charge forces create a balance between beam fields and wakefields that reduces beam energy spread and improves energy stability – both critical for beam extraction, transport, and focusing into a metre-scale undulator. Here, the resulting ultra-bright beams produce wavelength-tunable, coherent, femtosecond-scale photon pulses at strong gain. This regime enables reliable generation of multi-gigawatt-class X-ray laser pulses across the water window, offering tunability via the witness beam charge and robustness against variations in plasma wakefield strength and plasma photocathode laser jitter. Our findings help democratise access to coherent, high-power, soft X-ray radiation.

title: Non-van der Waals superlattices reconcile the strength and conductivity of MXene films
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Conventional strategies for assembling macroscopic MXene films require excessive binders, such as polymer chains or cellulose, to bridge adjacent nanosheets, which undermine intrinsic functionalities and reduce MXenes to mere conductive fillers. Here, we present a strategy that leverages the intrinsic structural evolution of MXenes to achieve non-van der Waals superlattice roll-ups, simultaneously enhancing interlayer stress transfer and establishing efficient conductive pathways, thereby overcoming the traditional trade-off between mechanical and electrical performance in MXene films. The resulting scalable high-performance MXene films exhibit remarkable tensile strength (598 MPa) and electrical conductivity (13682 S/cm), while also demonstrating excellent electromagnetic interference shielding. However, a systematic understanding on the reinforcement mechanisms across multiple scales is lacking which limits the rational design of high-performance MXene films. To address this, we systematically elucidate the complex reinforcement mechanisms across multiple scales, from crack deflection at the microscopic level, to dynamic slip and energy dissipation at the nanoscale, and local charge rearrangement through molecular interactions. This work establishes a multiscale blueprint for mechanical enhancement spanning microscopic, nanoscopic, and molecular regimes, representing a significant advance in the development of high-performance films.

title: Disrupting the semantic network shifts activity to domain-general brain regions
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Semantic processing relies on flexible interactions between specialized lexico-semantic regions and domain-general control networks, particularly under challenging conditions. Using transcranial magnetic stimulation interleaved with functional magnetic resonance imaging, we investigated acute network adaptation when the left posterior middle temporal gyrus—a core lexico-semantic region—was perturbed during lexico-semantic decisions in 25 healthy participants. High-intensity transcranial magnetic stimulation over the posterior middle temporal gyrus induced task-specific activity increases across semantic control and lexical retrieval areas, as well as remote domain-general regions. Critically, increased local activity at the stimulation site correlated with slower reaction times, whereas greater upregulation in domain-general frontal regions was associated with less disrupted semantic performance. These findings indicate that acute semantic disruption triggers immediate, flexible recruitment of domain-general control areas consistent with the maintenance of task performance, highlighting the brain’s capacity to dynamically adapt to interference. Our findings contribute to the current understanding of putative compensatory network-level mechanisms supporting lexico-semantic cognition.

title: Compound effects of traffic and climate on electric vehicle HVAC energy consumption: a spatiotemporal framework with city-level attribution
abstract: Real-world electric vehicle (EV) energy consumption can deviate by 20-40% from rated values, driven by ambient temperature, traffic congestion, and route characteristics. Existing studies treat these factors in isolation or as static loads, leaving the compound effect of co-varying climate and traffic on HVAC energy unquantified and per-route attribution unavailable. We develop a spatiotemporal simulation framework that couples traffic-aware driving speed, time- and location-specific ambient temperature, and physics-based submodels (cabin HVAC, traction, battery thermal management) at the segment level, paired with a regression-based decomposition that attributes HVAC variability to temperature and trip-duration components on a per-route basis. Applied through a factorial design across seven UK cities and eight radial routes from Manchester, the framework shows total energy varying by 14\% across cities while HVAC energy varies by up to 89\%, making cabin thermal management the primary differentiator under winter conditions. Trip duration, set by traffic and road type, is frequently the dominant driver of HVAC variability: in London, 83\% of above-average HVAC energy is attributable to congestion-extended trip time rather than to temperature. The decomposition yields a closed-form HVAC model from three inputs (ambient temperature, average speed, trip distance), with physically interpretable coefficients and straightforward transfer to other vehicles or regions through three coefficient re-fits. EV range variability is substantially shaped by traffic and road-network characteristics, with implications for route planning, infrastructure design, and energy equity.

title: A language model-informed minimalistic design of functional coacervate vesicles
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Hierarchical biopolymer interactions in nature yield intricate architectures, while synthetic biomimetics adopt a reductionist approach to create scalable and tunable systems. Inspired by intracellular liquid-liquid phase separation into membraneless, vesicle-like condensates, synthetic coacervate vesicles (CVs) have emerged for drug delivery, protocell design, and catalysis. However, a general reductionist framework for rationally constructing CVs remains challenging due to insufficient understanding of the minimal motifs required to drive coacervates into stable vesicular topologies. Here, we present a protein language model-informed design of such minimal systems, where arginine-rich oligopeptides and competing anionic oligomers self-assemble into oligo-coacervate vesicles (OCVs) without any chemical modifications or external fuels. Combining experiments and molecular dynamics simulations, we demonstrate an assembly mechanism governed by an electrostatic-hydrophobic balance, which enables vesiculation across a broad range of oligomer pairs. This principle further permits de novo functionalization, exemplified by OCVs engineered to selectively recognize and encapsulate DNA G-quadruplex structures. Together, these findings establish sequence-encoded design rules for the predictable construction of vesicle-like compartments.

title: Energy-guided combinatorial co-optimization of antibody affinity and stability
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Affinity maturation is an essential process in antibody engineering. Although powerful, it is iterative, time-consuming, and can result in trade-offs, where affinity is gained at the cost of important properties, such as specificity and stability. We present a scalable strategy, called LAffAb, that starts from a crystallographic structure of the antibody-antigen complex and introduces combinations of mutations to the antibody to optimize the energy of the complex. A combinatorial library comprising 7000 variants with up to nine mutations results in gains of up to 30-fold in affinity while co-optimizing stability. Surprisingly, the library does not converge on a single solution, instead favoring diverse variants with a high mutational load. Small-scale screening of 10 designs against a potential drug target improves affinity by an order-of-magnitude while maintaining high developability. We also apply LAffAb to improve the developability of a therapeutic antibody while maintaining affinity. We envision that LAffAb can be used to design stable, specific, and high-affinity binders and to improve our understanding of sequence, structure, and function relationships in antibodies.

title: Chemokine and opioid peptide scavenging through constitutive and ligand-induced release of ACKR3-bearing extracellular vesicles
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Atypical chemokine receptors (ACKRs) are non-signaling GPCRs that regulate ligand availability, with ACKR3 functioning as a dual scavenger of chemokines and opioid peptides. Here, we demonstrate that following ligand stimulation, besides the canonical internalization, ACKR3 is released on extracellular vesicles (EVs). ACKR3 was also found on EVs released under basal conditions, although to a lesser extent. These observations were confirmed across multiple cellular contexts, including endogenous systems. Mechanistically, basal and ligand-induced EV release are independent of GRKs and β-arrestin but each relies on different trafficking routes and C-terminal determinants. Ligand-induced EV release is associated with plasma membrane localization and receptor recycling pathways. In contrast, basal EV release is governed by intracellular sorting processes and influenced by receptor ubiquitination and RAMP3. Functionally, EV-associated ACKR3 retains high-affinity ligand binding, enabling sequestration of CXCL12 and opioid peptides and thereby attenuating their signaling through CXCR4 and MOR. We also show that the release on EVs, in particular under basal conditions, is observed for other receptors such as KOR, CXCR4 and several ACKRs. Collectively, these findings establish EVs as regulators in chemokine and opioid systems and as a distinct dimension of ACKR3 and more broadly GPCR biology.

title: Genomic language models decode bidirectional promoter activity and reveal conserved regulatory patterns across plant species
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Bidirectional promoters (BDPs), intergenic regions that coordinate transcription of oppositely oriented genes, pervade eukaryotic genomes, yet sequence signatures remain poorly defined. Existing approaches to BDP identification rely on distance thresholds and cannot infer activity from DNA. Here, we use Evo2, a genomic language model, to predict BDP activity and uncover sequence-encoded regulatory principles across four plant species (Arabidopsis, maize, rice, and wheat). We stratify BDPs by co-expression strength and compare Evo2-derived embeddings against k-mer profiles, transcription factor binding site matrices, and convolutional neural networks trained on sequence. Evo2 embeddings outperform all baselines, demonstrating that genomic language models capture regulatory information underlying BDP activity. Models trained on one or multiple species transfer to held-out species, and in planta validation in Spartina alterniflora confirms predicted high-activity BDPs. Sparse autoencoder analysis links Evo2 embeddings to nucleosome positioning and species-specific transcription factor landscapes, providing insight into sequence determinants underlying BDP activity . This work establishes how genomic language models can extract bidirectional promoter logic from sequence and identify conserved regulatory rules across plants.

title: The modular evolution of chitinases is governed by coevolution of auxiliary and catalytic domains
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The modular architecture of multi-domain enzymes is a key source of functional diversity. GH18 chitinases exemplify this, possessing a variety of auxiliary domains that have been postulated to underpin their role as essential global nutrient cyclers. However, there is no evolutionary framework that accounts for the vast assortment of domain compositions observed across the protein family. Here, we map the sequence space of prokaryotic chitinases, integrating phylogenetics with a quantitative analysis of domain promiscuity to decode their evolutionary history. We reveal that diversification follows distinct trajectories: enzymes necessary for environmental chitin scavenging evolve via high modular plasticity and structural elaboration of the catalytic core, whereas sequences required for specialized, essential developmental roles fix their domain architecture to fulfil lineage-specific physiological roles. By resolving how domain accretion co-evolves with catalytic scaffolds, this work provides a framework for understanding how multi-domain enzymes adapt to complex environments.

title: Effective enzyme engineering through modeling kinetic parameter changes upon mutations with geometric deep learning
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Quantifying enzyme kinetic parameter changes upon mutations is essential for accelerating enzyme evolution. Current methods focus on predicting absolute values of kinetic parameters (turnover numbers kcat and Michaelis constants Km), yet they fail to accurately capture mutation effects. To our knowledge, no method directly models mutation effects (Δkcat and ΔKm) due to the scarcity of such training data. Moreover, these methods haven’t fully exploited protein structural geometry. Here, we establish a high-quality enzyme mutation effect dataset by pairing wild-type and mutant kinetic parameters measured under identical experimental conditions via a semi-automatic procedure combining language model-assisted parsing and manual verification. Leveraging this dataset, we develop DeltaCata, a Siamese geometric graph neural network to directly predict the changes in kinetic parameters induced by residue substitutions. DeltaCata demonstrates substantial performance improvements over existing methods, especially for enzymes unseen in the training sets. Its utility is further validated through in silico beneficial mutation screening experiments using deep mutational scanning datasets. Finally, we apply DeltaCata to engineer the methyltransferase sGmOMT2, achieving up to a 7.0-fold improvement in catalytic efficiency for in vitro icaritin synthesis. These results suggest the high potential of DeltaCata for industrial enzyme engineering.

title: Engineering filamentous myosins for optical control of contractility
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Understanding the behaviors of contractile actomyosin systems requires precise spatiotemporal control of filamentous myosin activity. Here, we develop a tool for optical control of contractility by extending the MyLOV family of gearshifting motors to create engineered filamentous myosins that change velocity in response to blue light. We characterize these minifilaments using in vitro single-molecule tracking assays, contractility assays in reconstituted actin networks, and imaging of contractile phenotypes in live cells. In vitro, gearshifting minifilaments change speed and/or direction when illuminated, and contraction rates of minifilaments in actin networks can be modulated using blue light. In cells, gearshifting minifilaments enable optical control of protrusion retraction, cortical flow, and cell migration. Finally, we develop an alternative design for minifilaments that only interact processively with actin in blue light. Engineered minifilaments could be used to dissect behaviors such as self-organization and mechanotransduction in contractile systems both in vitro and in cells and tissues.

title: Pulsed photoelectrocatalysis enables efficient urea synthesis over Cu(salen)-COF
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Electrocatalytic urea synthesis from carbon dioxide and nitrate under ambient conditions offers a sustainable alternative to the energy-intensive Bosch-Meiser process. However, its efficiency is constrained by the spatiotemporal mismatch of key carbon and nitrogen intermediates at the catalyst-electrolyte interface. Herein, we address this limitation through interfacial microenvironment optimization combining ionic liquid modification of copper-salen covalent organic framework, pulsed electrolysis, and photoelectrocatalytic coupling. The ionic liquid modification enriches carbon dioxide and facilitates interfacial charge transfer, pulsed electrolysis promotes the dynamic matching of carbon and nitrogen intermediates, and photoelectrocatalytic coupling boosts interfacial electron accumulation. The integrated system achieves a urea yield rate of 69.2 mmol gcat−1 h−1 with a Faradaic efficiency of 56.7% in an H-type cell and 82.5% in a flow cell. In this work, we establish a generalizable strategy for efficient urea electrosynthesis via hierarchical interfacial control and highlight the potential of pulsed photoelectrocatalysis.

title: Toward Ternary Computing Enabled by Origami-Inspired Modular Architectures
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Modern mechanical computing, being envisioned as a pathway toward structure- and material-level processing, holds potential for intelligent metamaterials and robotics in extreme environments. However, current computing architectures remain constrained by binary paradigms. Here, we introduce an origami-inspired modular architecture that encodes logical mappings into its inherent kinematic responses under an input-output decoupled paradigm, enabling both binary and ternary mechanical computing. Within this emerging paradigm, the multi-stable states of two Kresling origami configurations serve as physical carriers for generating discrete signals, while torsional transitions among these states ensure signal switching, supporting operations from logic gates to advanced arithmetic. Based on this mechanical architecture, we systematically demonstrate seven common logic gates and modular arithmetic half- and full-adders in both binary and ternary systems, revealing challenges and opportunities in advancing multi-valued logic through comparative analysis. The physical platform, along with its accompanying response-programming strategy, represents a simplified and generalized paradigm that supports migration to higher-level mechanical computing mechanisms.

title: Count the climate losses we prevent
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Climate adaptation reduces losses, but successful risk reduction often leaves no claim or expenditure that records the benefit. Avoided-loss accounts would preserve intervention-specific estimates and evidence across insurance, lending and public finance, without recognizing counterfactual losses as assets.

title: Recent extreme heatwaves are no match for future events
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: In recent years, record-breaking heatwaves have occurred over many regions of the Earth causing serious impacts to human and natural systems. Here we show that recently observed exceptional heatwaves are no match to potential future 21st century events based on multiple metrics. For several observed heatwaves, this holds even under low- and medium-emissions scenarios. In a high- to very high-emissions future, many regions are projected to experience heatwaves that generate several times more cumulative heat and are many times longer (up to several months) than the observed heatwaves. Should the Nationally Determined Contributions under the Paris Agreement not be implemented, in most regions a concerningly large proportion of projected heatwaves exceeds all analyzed heatwave characteristics at once. Our results underscore the crucial need for substantial emissions reduction and have important implications for adaptation measures, as a substantial proportion of projected heatwaves is well outside the recent lived experience.

title: Daily briefing: Toothbrush zaps bacteria to clear plaque
abstract: The manual toothbrush cleans by generating a bacteria-killing electrical charge. Plus, what ‘historic’ US mid-term results mean for science and a genetics lab run by AI-powered robots.

title: Diacylglycerol Metabolism Drives Host–pathogen Responses During Enteric Infection in Drosophila
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Lipid metabolism is fundamental to cellular homeostasis, supporting energy storage, membrane architecture, and cellular signaling. Beyond these canonical roles, lipids have emerged as critical regulators of host immunity. Here, we define a lipid-driven mechanism that governs host–pathogen interactions by impacting pathogen clearance and thus infection outcomes. Exploiting Drosophila, we show that enteric infection triggers robust accumulation of neutral lipids, and specifically 1,2-diacylglycerols (DAGs), in the midgut. Disruption of DAG biosynthesis or lipid transport in midgut enterocytes (ECs) impairs lipid accumulation and reduces host survival. Conversely, dietary lipid supplementation enhances lipid storage and improves survival. Mechanistically, these lipid-dependent responses regulate defecation, thereby controlling bacterial clearance from the midgut. DAGs can act as signaling lipids that activate protein kinase C (PKC), and DAG accumulation in ECs correlates with elevated PKC activity and calcium signaling in midgut visceral muscle (VM), promoting VM contraction, midgut motility, and expulsion of pathogens via defecation. Together, our findings reveal a previously unrecognized role for DAG metabolism in shaping host defenses.

title: Electrolyte-dependent physico-chemical interfacial kinetics shape degradation pathways and lifetime in lithium-ion batteries
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Electrolyte-dependent lifetime variability remains a major obstacle to sustainable deployment of lithium-ion batteries, contributing to premature retirement, increased material demand and uncertainty in lifecycle assessment. However, most continuum degradation models represent the electrolyte through bulk transport, without capturing its role in interfacial degradation. Here, we use customised multi-layer pouch cells with varied ethylene carbonate:dimethyl carbonate ratio, lithium hexafluorophosphate concentration and electrolyte amount to examine how electrolyte conditions shape degradation trajectories under accelerated degradation. Within this formulation framework, changing the solvent ratio leads to distinct lifetime trajectories across otherwise comparable cells. Electrochemical diagnostics, gas analysis and post-mortem interfacial characterisation show that this divergence is associated with electrolyte-sensitive interphase growth, parasitic reactions and spatially heterogeneous surface degradation. We incorporate electrolyte-dependent transport and thermodynamic properties into a physics-based degradation model. A transport-only implementation does not reproduce the observed separation in capacity-retention trajectories. Introducing a minimal electrolyte-sensitive refinement through an effective interphase transport parameter improves agreement in the ethylene-carbonate-rich case. These results identify electrolyte-sensitive interfacial degradation as a necessary modelling dimension for reliable lifetime prediction.

title: Silicon photonics provides a unified solution for all-distance optical communications
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Optical links underpin global communications from chip-to-chip interconnects to transoceanic fibre networks. Conventional architectures remain distance-dependent: long-haul systems rely on coherent transmission for high spectral efficiency and capacity, while short-reach links favour intensity modulation due to hardware complexity and power constraints. This divide impedes scalability for AI-driven intra-data-centre traffic and low-latency, flexible cloud-to-edge connectivity. Here we demonstrate a unified silicon photonic coherent solution for all-distance optical communications. By employing an ultralow-loss silicon nitride external cavity, we achieve 70 mW of direct laser output with a sub-kHz linewidth and 13.7% wall-plug efficiency. Paired with silicon photonic transceivers, this platform enables short-distance transmission without optical amplification across 256 wavelength channels, corresponding to an aggregate data rate of 81.92 Tb/s, as well as transmission exceeding 4400 km. It also supports wavelength switching and transmission re-establishment at tens-of-microseconds timescales. These results indicate the potential to simplify optical interfaces and enable flexible wavelength-routed connectivity.

title: Regulating glycerol electrooxidation pathways via catalytic environments
abstract: A step-resolved framework explains how catalytic environments regulate adsorption, dehydrogenation, chemical conversion, C–C cleavage and desorption to shape glycerol electrooxidation selectivity, activity and stability.

title: Multiscale neural dynamics reveal how striatal subregions shape stress vulnerability and resilience
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Effective stress coping relies on neural and endocrine coordination, with the mesostriatal system serving as a central substrate. However, how striatal subregions contribute to stress vulnerability versus resilience remains unclear. Here, we show dissociable roles of the nucleus accumbens (NAC) and dorsal caudate (dCA) and their associated brain networks in shaping stress responses. We identify neural stability (NS)—capturing stress-induced changes in state-switching frequency over the course of stress responses—as a marker: task-state NS correlates positively with stress-related NAC activity, whereas resting-state NS correlates inversely with stress-related dCA activity. NAC-mediated networks and associated NS further predict faster cortisol recovery. Intriguingly, NAC-related functional connectivity patterns spatially covary with dopamine D2 receptor distributions and gene expression in inhibitory neurons and glia, whereas dCA-related patterns covary with μ-opioid receptor distributions. Together, these findings reveal striatal subregional heterogeneity in stress coping and characterize resilience as a multisystem homeostatic process integrating neural, endocrine, and molecular layers.

title: Two distinct α2β1 integrin glycan interactions mediate cell entry of a picornavirus
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Equine rhinitis A virus (ERAV), a picornavirus closely related to foot-and-mouth disease virus, causes respiratory infections in horses. We performed a HEK293T CRISPRi screen and identified integrin α2β1 as a protein receptor for ERAV. Using knock-out cells and pretreating cells with an antibody or soluble receptor, we confirmed the importance of this integrin for infection of multiple cell types, including equine fibroblasts. Cryo-EM and glycoproteomics analyses revealed that ERAV binds integrin α2β1 in its closed conformation by attaching to the β-propeller of the α2 chain, independent of divalent cations, as well as to a high-mannose glycan on α2 N112 and a sialylated glycan on β1 N269. Using glycan knockout and knock-in cells and by reconstituting integrin α2β1-depleted cells with mutant receptors, we demonstrated the importance of these glycans for virus entry. Our results identify a hitherto unseen combination of protein and glycan interactions between a virus and its receptor.

title: Model systems and integration strategies to capture human biology
abstract: Modelling human biology is difficult precisely because many of the responses that matter most emerge not within a single tissue or cell type, but at the boundaries where matrix, immune and systemic signals converge in ways that are hard to recreate in isolation. Conventional in vitro systems and animal studies have advanced our understanding of many physiological processes, but they still consistently fall short at these interfaces. In this Review, we discuss how engineered materials, organoids, microphysiological systems and computational models can be used together to build more informative human model systems. We first consider engineered materials as tools for controlling the local environment around cells, including matrix composition, stiffness, geometry, transport and time-dependent cues. We then examine organoids, assembloids and microphysiological system platforms, with emphasis on functional benchmarking, vascularization, immune integration, maturation, reproducibility and biological variation across donors and conditions. Finally, we discuss computational models, including spatial atlases, generative models and digital twins, as tools for organizing measurements, testing mechanisms and improving prediction. A key insight is that no current platform fully closes the loop between sensing, tissue modelling, computational calibration and feedback-guided intervention. The central challenge now is to build models whose complexity is justified by the human question they are designed to answer.

title: Mechanical adaptation drives out-of-equilibrium network reorganization and self-strengthening in adapt-ring networks
abstract: Synthetic polymer networks typically lack the ability to autonomously remodel and strengthen under mechanical stress, a capability commonly observed in natural materials. Here we introduce adapt-ring networks (ARNs) that establish a general design principle for adaptive polymer materials. ARNs couple a covalent polyethylene glycol network with reconfigurable α-cyclodextrin crystalline domains whose strain-directed fragmentation, translocation and alignment form kinetically trapped architectures encoding local mechanical history. Mechanical training enhances Young's modulus, tensile strength, fracture energy and fatigue threshold by up to an order of magnitude, with full reversibility through solvent-induced crystalline-domain reformation. Spatially resolved adaptation and 3D printability enable gradient materials and customized architectures. Incorporating polyethylene glycol side chains to form dangling-chain ARNs enables strain-controlled out-of-equilibrium growth through threading and crystallization of external α-cyclodextrins. These hydrogels autonomously generate spatially self-organized, strain-dependent reinforcement, including non-local, environment-fed stiffening conceptually analogous to biological reinforcement. These features establish a general approach to bio-inspired, non-equilibrium soft materials that adapt, remember, regrow and readapt.

title: Liquid metal biomimetics: a chemical perspective
abstract: A chemistry-centered framework for Ga-based liquid metal biomimetics, linking multiscale material design and interfacial reactions to matter simulation, energy conversion, information processing and cross-habitat adaptation.

title: Gas Retention in Porous Cathodes Governs Bicarbonate Electrolysis Performance
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Bicarbonate electrolysis offers a direct route for converting captured CO2 into high-value chemicals without energy-intensive CO2 regeneration and compression. However, multiphase transport within liquid-fed porous cathodes remains poorly understood. We found carbon paper and carbon cloth yielded drastically different performance, and further analysis revealed gas retention, i.e., localized and temporary entrapment of internally generated gas within the pore network, as an important transport limitation. Flow pulse and recovery experiments under galvanostatic operations showed largely reversible performance losses, while operando X-ray imaging directly visualized gas retention. Gas retention intensifies with denser electrodes, lower catholyte flow rates, and higher current densities. Guided by these observations, an interdigitated flow field was employed to enhance through-plane convection and gas removal, increasing the maximum formate partial current density to 304 mA cm–2 and enabling 120 h of stable operation. These findings establish gas management as a critical design criterion for bicarbonate electrolyzers.

title: Chiral Two-Dimensional Perovskite Single Crystals Enable Flexible Piezoelectric Nanogenerators for High-Sensitivity Ultrasound Detection
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hybrid perovskites are emerging as promising piezoelectric materials, yet the use of high-quality single crystals in flexible ultrasound sensing remains largely unexplored. Here, we report intrinsically noncentrosymmetric chiral two-dimensional perovskite single crystals, (S/R-NEA)2PbBr4, that exhibit strong piezoelectricity arising from chirality-induced symmetry breaking and enhanced lattice polarizability. By integrating these crystals into a polymer matrix, we realize flexible piezoelectric nanogenerators delivering high output (∼8 V) under ultrasonic excitation. The devices enable reliable detection and clear resolution of 50 kHz ultrasound signals, along with excellent mechanical durability and environmental stability. This work establishes a single-crystal strategy for flexible piezoelectric devices and highlights chiral 2D perovskites as a compelling platform for high-sensitivity ultrasound detection and energy harvesting.

title: Resident cardiac macrophage-like cells induced by an ILC2 cytokine cocktail confer cardioprotection through enhanced efferocytosis in a mouse model of myocardial infarction
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Resident cardiac macrophages (RCM) are essential for myocardial repair following acute myocardial infarction (AMI); however, their therapeutic application is hindered by limited availability. Here, we show that RCM transplantation from healthy mice markedly attenuates cardiac injury in mice. Importantly, we identify a pro-reparative CD301b⁺ RCM population profoundly depleted after AMI and show that adoptive transfer of this subset alone mitigates cardiac injury following myocardial infarction. To overcome the scarcity of native RCMs and favour their replenishment, we expand ex vivo a CD301b+ macrophage-like population (RCML) by polarizing bone marrow-derived macrophages with an ILC2-derived cytokine cocktail, and show that RCML transplantation confers robust post-AMI cardioprotection. Mechanistically, CD301b promotes efferocytosis by enhancing TFEB-mediated lysosomal function via a GATM-AMPK-mTOR axis, a pathway conserved in human macrophages. Thus, our findings identify a key pro-reparative macrophage subset and establish a feasible cell-based strategy for cardiac repair.

title: Pathology-adapted peptide–oligonucleotide nanohybrid mitigates glucocorticoid-induced bone loss
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Glucocorticoid-induced bone loss (GIBL) remains a major clinical challenge, manifested by both systemic osteopenia and osteonecrosis of the femoral head under chronic glucocorticoid exposure, yet current therapies are limited in coordinately addressing bone deterioration and vascular impairment. With advances in precision medicine, oligonucleotide therapeutics offer opportunities for pathophysiology-informed intervention. Here, we report a pathology-adapted peptide-oligonucleotide nanohybrid (PON) developed for targeted miR-26a-5p delivery to glucocorticoid-injured bone. By integrating self-assembly, bone targeting, enzyme responsiveness, cell penetration, and lysosomal escape, PONs were designed to incorporate pathology-responsive delivery features and address key barriers to oligonucleotide delivery. Mechanistically, PON-mediated miR-26a-5p delivery reduced GSK-3β expression and promoted HIF-1α stabilization, thereby preserving osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling and attenuating apoptosis. In a rat model of GIBL, systemic PON administration protects against early skeletal and vascular injury and limits progression after disease establishment. These findings identify the therapeutic relevance of miR-26a-5p in GIBL, and support the potential of PON system for bone-targeted oligonucleotide therapy.

title: Distributed range adaptation in human parietal encoding of numbers
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The brain’s representations are encoded in the collective activity of neural populations whose non-monotonic tuning properties define the population code. Adaptive behavior calls for flexible retuning of this code as stimulus statistics change across contexts. Yet how such adaptation occurs is unknown. Using fMRI during a numerosity-estimation task with variable number ranges, we show that number representations in human parietal cortex dynamically recalibrate to context, enabling context-sensitive behavioral accuracy. The tuning properties of neural populations collectively shift and rescale with the range. This distributed range adaptation achieves efficient coding in real time: neural precision scales with the range and predicts corresponding changes in behavioral precision. Individuals with stronger neural adaptation show larger behavioral adjustments. These findings extend static sensory efficient coding to adaptive representations of abstract magnitudes. Such flexible population tuning may constitute a canonical mechanism of encoding networks that enables the brain to sustain precise, adaptive behavior.

title: Atomically resolved exciton emission from single defects in MoS2
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Excitons, bound electron–hole pairs, govern the optical response of semiconductors and underpin technologies ranging from photovoltaics to quantum light sources. In nanoscale systems, the spatial extent of excitons approaches atomic dimensions, yet direct imaging of excitonic processes in real space has remained elusive. Two-dimensional semiconductors such as transition metal dichalcogenides provide a platform where reduced screening, high light extraction and atomically defined defect sites enable the exploration of exciton physics at atomic length scales. However, the microscopic origin of defect-related emission and its variability across samples have remained debated. Here we show that scanning tunnelling microscopy-induced luminescence reveals the atomic and optical fingerprints of individual defects in monolayer MoS
                    2
                    . Decoupling the material from its substrate using bilayer hexagonal boron nitride enables the detection of sharp excitonic emission and spatially localized defect emission, which we attribute to free-to-bound recombination (
                    e
                    ,A
                    0
                    ), and map its distribution with subnanometre-resolved fluorescence imaging. We identify negatively charged carbon–hydrogen complexes as the defect species responsible for a ubiquitous defect emission band in MoS
                    2
                    . These results provide atomically resolved images of exciton emission in a solid-state material, linking atomic defect structure to its optical fingerprint and establishing a microscopic basis for deterministic quantum emitter engineering in two-dimensional materials.

title: Repurposed endogenous virus-like vesicles mediate dendritic cell long-range antigen presentation and T cell activation for enhanced cancer vaccination
abstract: Dendritic cells release extracellular vesicles (DEVs) that amplify antigen presentation while incorporating patient-derived, rapidly evolving antigens. By enriching peptide-major histocompatibility complex (MHC) and co-stimulatory ligands orders of magnitude above donor-cell levels, DEVs emerge as potent vesicle-vaccines, although efficacy remains limited by unclear mechanisms. Here we show that dendritic cells repurpose the virus-like retrotransposon-derived Arc gene to generate endogenous virus-like vesicles (VLVs) that predominantly carry peptide-MHC and high-density co-stimulatory ligands, intensifying and extending antigen presentation. Upon antigen exposure, Arc partners with endogenous envelope proteins to assemble VLVs that directly engage T cells and trigger intrinsic adjuvanticity via viral mimicry. DEVs lacking Arc failed to prime antigen-specific T cell responses, whereas Arc overexpression shifted DEVs toward VLVs that trafficked to lymphoid organs, drove rapid CD4-assisted priming and durable CD8-biased memory, suppressed melanoma, and prolonged survival. Our data reveal a viral-mimicry mechanism enabling long-range immune activation and support Arc+ VLVs as an antigen-agnostic vaccine for cancer immunotherapy.

title: Cold Atmospheric Plasma–Enabled SiO x Nanocoatings for Surface Energy Modulation and Enhanced Seed Germination
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Modern agricultural systems demand higher and more reliable yields under increasing constraints on land, water, and fertilizer inputs. Rapid and uniform seed germination is therefore critical for improving crop establishment and overall yield performance. Although existing strategies, such as ionizing gas treatments, polymer coatings, and nanoparticle-based seed treatments, can enhance water uptake and early vigor, they often suffer from limited stability, processing complexity, or potential seed damage. Here, we introduce a dry, cold atmospheric plasma (CAP)-assisted deposition platform for the conformal SiOx nanocoating of seeds, enabling a hydrophilic, storage-stable surface modification under ambient conditions. The deposition process was systematically optimized to achieve rapid, uniform coating formation directly on the seed surface. As a model system, corn seeds (Zea mays L.) were coated with SiOx nanofilms under optimized conditions. Wettability analysis revealed a ∼4-fold reduction in the static water contact angle for SiOx-coated seeds relative to pristine controls, compared with a ∼2.9-fold reduction for plasma-treated seeds without precursor introduction. Importantly, the SiOx-induced hydrophilicity exhibited superior stability, showing less than 3° contact angle recovery after 21 days of storage, whereas plasma-treated seeds alone displayed ∼50° recovery within 120 h. This stable and enhanced surface hydrophilicity translated into accelerated germination and improved early seedling vigor, resulting in SiOx-coated seeds exhibiting improved total seedling growth immediately after treatment and maintaining an approximately 38% increase compared with pristine controls after storage, demonstrating consistent storage stability. In comparison, the early-germination and seedling-growth advantages of plasma-treated seeds diminished substantially after storage, indicating that CAP-deposited SiOx provides a more persistent and storage-stable functional modification. Collectively, these results establish CAP-deposited SiOx nanocoatings as a scalable, solvent-free nanotechnology platform for stabilizing seed hydrophilicity, accelerating germination, and promoting early seedling growth under agronomically relevant conditions.

title: Endogenous virus-like extracellular vesicles enhance the efficacy of cancer vaccines
abstract: Harnessing viral mimicry mechanisms enhances cancer vaccination by improving long-range antigen presentation and T cell activation.

title: Opportunistically Detecting Signs of Hypertension on a Consumer Smartwatch
abstract: Hypertension is a silent killer, with over half of affected adults unaware of their condition1,2. This lack of awareness is a major concern, as early intervention is critical for preventing major adverse cardiovascular events3,4. Here we show that applying artificial intelligence (AI) to multimodal waveforms (photoplethysmography and accelerometry) recorded using a widely available consumer smartwatch (AI-PPG-ACC-HTN), without any cuff calibration, can detect hypertension with accuracy levels comparable to traditional cuffed blood pressure (BP) devices in the existing clinical framework. We validated AI-PPG-ACC-HTN in a prospective, multicenter study of 196 diverse participants free from known cardiovascular disease and antihypertensive medication against gold-standard 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring. Over seven days of real-world monitoring, AI-PPG-ACC-HTN detected hypertension with a sensitivity of 65.8% (95% CI, 54.0%-76.3%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%), and positive predictive value (PPV) of 80.6% (95% CI, 68.6%-89.6%). In comparison, initial office BP screening achieved a sensitivity of 55.3% (95% CI, 43.4%-66.7%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%) and PPV of 77.8% (95% CI, 64.4%-88.0%). These results highlight an opportunity for consumer smartwatches to facilitate population-level opportunistic hypertension screening by prompting at-risk individuals toward clinical assessment and confirmatory diagnosis using established cuff-based methodologies, offering an accessible tool to address this major public health challenge.

title: Hydrogen Derivatives Enable Cost-Effective Carbon Neutrality in China
abstract: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change recommended 1.5°C carbon reduction target, requiring powerful enforcement from major economies. China, the largest CO2 emitter, is facing severe difficulties for both variable renewable accommodation and decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors. Hydrogen, as a critical green energy carrier bridging renewable to end-users, faces significant obstacles in real-world deployment such as costly transportation, storage and fuel-cell adoption. Affordable and coordinated hydrogen deployment plan to accelerate the carbon-neutral transition remains ambiguous. Here, we present cost-effective carbon-neutral transition pathways for entire energy economy of China emphasizing the significant role of hydrogen and derivatives as green energy carriers, considering high-resolution renewable deployments, hourly power system operations in 29 provincial regions, over 46,000 rail/road/marine/pipeline transfer routing of hydrogen derivatives, process-level fuel adoption strategies in all end-use sectors. Results show that incorporating hydrogen and derivatives can reduce the overall transition cost by $ 10.7 trillion compared with renewable and electrification pathways, achieving negative carbon abatement costs ($-6.15/ton), eliminating external oil import expenses, equivalent to over 50% of China trade surplus (2023 level)1, significantly boosting employment and economic growth. Hydrogen derivative based transition pathway offers a vital direction for affordable and secure decarbonization for China and beyond under volatile international energy markets.

title: Engineered Dielectric Response of Liquid-Filled Interfacial Bubbles in van der Waals Heterostructures
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Interfacial bubbles in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures are typically regarded as unavoidable byproducts of stacking. Here, we show that they can be repurposed as engineered dielectric nanocavities by intentionally trapping selected liquids during assembly. A simple prewetting step before stamp transfer forms liquid-filled bubbles at hBN/graphite interfaces containing acetone, ethanol, H2O, and NaCl(aq), alongside untreated reference bubbles. Electrostatic force microscopy (EFM), crosstalk correction, and finite-element modeling enable quantitative extraction of the effective dielectric constant (εeff) of individual bubbles, revealing higher εeff for all liquid-filled bubbles than for untreated ones. To estimate the apparent core permittivity of the confined contents, each bubble is modeled as a liquid core enclosed by an hBN shell. Simulations of the tip–bubble–substrate geometry yield core dielectric constants (εcore) larger than εeff yet physically consistent with the trapped media. Acetone and ethanol exhibit εcore values close to their expected dielectric properties, whereas water shows a reduced εcore consistent with nanoconfined pure water. Notably, NaCl(aq) shows a larger εcore than pure water, suggesting distinct electrolyte dielectric behavior under nanoscale confinement. This work establishes vdW bubbles as versatile platforms for engineering local electrostatic functionality and probing confined-liquid dielectric physics in two-dimensional (2D) material assemblies.

title: Controlling Compensation Doping via Multivalent Platinum Acceptors in Tantalum Oxide Thin Films
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Heterostructures of platinum (Pt) and tantalum oxide (Ta2O5) find widespread use in electronic and energy-conversion device applications, yet the electronic role of Pt incorporated within Ta2O5 remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the influence of Pt incorporation on the electronic structure and properties of amorphous Ta2O5 using two precisely controlled ternary atomic layer deposition (ALD) pathways. Oxygen plasma-enhanced deposition produces host matrices with significantly lower native defect and impurity concentrations than conventional thermal water-based ALD, enabling a systematic investigation of the interplay between Pt dopants and native defects. Controlled Pt incorporation over the range of 0.9–1.9 atom % yields homogeneous, amorphous Pt-doped Ta2O5 thin films containing exclusively Pt(II) and Pt(IV) oxidation states, with no evidence of metallic Pt formation. While the optical bandgap of the Ta2O5 host matrix remains largely unchanged, Pt incorporation introduces optically active acceptor states near the valence band maximum, increases sub-bandgap absorption, and shifts the Fermi level toward the midgap. The relative Pt(II)/Pt(IV) population depends strongly on the defect landscape of the host matrix and exhibits a linear dependence on the Fermi level position, demonstrating Fermi level-controlled charge compensation between native donor defects and multivalent Pt acceptor states. Density functional theory corroborates the acceptor character of Pt and assigns the introduced states primarily to Pt 5d orbitals. Experimentally constructed band diagrams and charge transport measurements further show that Pt incorporation provides a direct means of tuning the electronic properties of Ta2O5. These results demonstrate that multivalent Pt doping serves as a controllable strategy for engineering the electronic structure and transport characteristics of functional Ta2O5 thin films, with direct relevance to memristive, dielectric, and photoelectrochemical devices.

title: Translating EU renewable energy community policy under geopolitical constraint: An actor-network analysis of Cyprus
abstract: We use an actor-network concept of translation to examine how EU Renewable Energy Community (REC) policy translates into domestic practice under contested sovereignty, infrastructural isolation, and active geopolitical obstruction. Cyprus is a critical, theory-building case: the EU's last fully isolated grid, occupation of part of its territory by a third state, and Turkish obstruction of both gas exploitation and electricity interconnection make the assumptions embedded in EU policy unusually visible. Drawing on policy documents, twelve interviews and participant observation, we trace how the framework fragments as it moves from supranational design to local implementation. The evidence supports two case-derived hypotheses. The first, presupposition-mismatched translation, holds that compliance fails not for want of will or capacity but because the policy as written presupposes a context that does not exist locally, so translation fragments into competing local interpretations. The second, symmetric foreclosure, holds that where one external mechanism blocks both the domestically prioritised energy-security pathway (gas) and the EU-aligned pathway (interconnected renewable generation), competing local obligatory passage points cancel rather than converge. Their joint product is structural decoupling under material constraint, extending Bromley and Powell's means–ends decoupling to cases where the formal-substantive gap is produced by foreclosure of the prescribed means rather than by organizational choice. The argument is not that RECs cannot exist in Cyprus, but that this decarbonisation initiative receives weak domestic backing for geopolitical rather than technical reasons. We draw implications for green-transition initiatives in other peripheral, geopolitically exposed member states and for differentiated EU implementation guidance.

title: Low-Solvent Mechanochemical MOF Carrier Nanoarchitectonics for Targeted Quercetin Delivery for Dual-Mode ROS and Anti-inflammation Protection against LPS-Induced Acute Lung Injury
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nowadays, inhalable administration of nanomedicines is an appealing concept for acute lung injury (ALI). For ALI nanomedicine, it is appealing to achieve targeted delivery and on-demand release in the ALI microenvironment, which is acidic, rich in reactive oxygen species (ROS), and with elevated inflammatory mediator levels. Notably, customized metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) could fulfill these requirements and thus are promising nanocarriers for ALI medicine delivery, but MOFs formulated often suffer from unreacted residues with hazardous risk. Herein, we report a low-solvent mechanochemical synthesis method to formulate cerium-doped zeolitic imidazolate frameworks (Ce-ZIFs) stabilized by Pluronic F127 as drug delivery nanocarriers to load quercetin for targeted preventive ALI therapy. The nanoplatform exhibits robust structural integrity, high drug loading capacity, excellent biocompatibility, and pH-responsive release of quercetin under acidic conditions, mimicking the inflamed lung microenvironment. Importantly, the nanoplatform ameliorates pro-inflammatory mediators (TNF-α, IL-6), inhibits pulmonary edema, and attenuates alveolar injury in an LPS-induced ALI mouse model. Notably, Ce/ZIF promotes the Ce+3/Ce+4 redox process to generate catalase-like activity for catalytic reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging and sustainable antioxidant properties. Transcriptome sequencing and biological validation also revealed that the nanoplatform showed its remarkable ability to counteract LPS-induced oxidative damage and inflammatory responses by suppressing Th1 cell polarization.
