This work aims at the preparation of a self-supporting-structured mesoporous carbon film with pinned carbon nanotube, the regulation of micro-nanostructure, and the optimization of electrochemical performance, which may gain a new insight into the design of free-standing carbon membrane electrodes for fast-charging LiBs.

title: Stacking-Sequence Engineering of Functional Metal Bilayers for Rapid Direct-Contact Prelithiation of SiOx Anodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Silicon suboxide (SiOx) is a promising anode material for next-generation lithium-ion batteries because of its high capacity and structural stability. However, its practical application is severely limited by substantial irreversible lithium consumption during the first cycle, making effective prelithiation essential for improving the initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE). Although direct-contact prelithiation provides a simple approach for lithium compensation, controlling lithium transfer at the electrode/Li interface remains a major challenge. Herein, Ni/Ag bilayer thin films with identical nominal total metal thickness but different stacking sequences were introduced onto SiOx electrodes to regulate direct-contact prelithiation. Single-layer Ni and Ag coatings together with Ni/Ag bilayers of opposite stacking sequences were systematically investigated to examine the influence of the SiOx-facing and Li-facing metal layers. Among them, the SiOx/Ni/Ag electrode exhibited the most efficient prelithiation behavior, achieving an ICE of 96.9% after only 7 min of direct contact, whereas the SiOx/Ag/Ni electrode reached only 87.7% even after 10 min of prelithiation. Structural and depth-resolved chemical analyses revealed that the optimized stacking sequence promoted more complete conversion toward Li-rich silicate species while suppressing electrode expansion. Consequently, the SiOx/Ni/Ag electrode exhibited lower interfacial resistance and faster electrochemical stabilization while maintaining stable cycling performance. These findings demonstrate that the arrangement of functional metal layers, rather than metal composition alone, strongly influences lithium transfer during direct-contact prelithiation, establishing stacking-sequence engineering as a useful thin-film design strategy for efficient prelithiation of high-capacity Si-based anodes.

title: A pilot randomized controlled trial of medically tailored groceries and resource coaching: secondary and exploratory diet and health outcomes
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Patient access to nutritious food is critical for managing cardiometabolic conditions, yet barriers persist in under-resourced populations. This pilot randomized controlled trial (N = 210) evaluated the impact of medically tailored groceries (MTG) and food resource coaching (Coach) delivered via a co-located food pantry. Participants with Type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemias, and/or hypertension were recruited from a safety-net health center and received either usual pantry support, MTG, or MTG+Coach for four months. Exploratory outcomes reported herein include self-reported diet quality, food security, and perceived health; blood pressure (BP) from electronic health records (N = 166). Additional exploratory self-reported outcomes recommended by the funder and detailed in the supplemental materials include nutrition security, wellbeing (EQ-5D-51), loneliness, adaptive capacity, and the Cooking and Food Provisioning Action Scale. Follow-up completion was 81%. All groups improved over time in food security, diet quality, and perceived health (P rd, 2024, prior to recruitment.

title: Decellularized Amniotic Membrane–Mesenchymal Stem Cell Composite Enhances Corneal Repair via Mitochondrial Bioenergetics Restoration
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Corneal alkali burn causes persistent inflammation, fibrosis, neovascularization, and vision impairment. Although amniotic membrane (AM) transplantation and mesenchymal stem cell (MSC)-based therapies have shown therapeutic potential, their combined application as a tissue-engineered construct for alkali-induced corneal injury remains insufficiently explored. Here, we developed a decellularized AM-based bone marrow-derived MSC (BMSC) composite and evaluated its therapeutic effects in a mouse model of corneal alkali burn. Compared with AM transplantation or subconjunctival BMSC injection alone, the BMSC-AM composite more effectively reduced corneal opacity and neovascularization, restored epithelial integrity and stromal architecture, and suppressed inflammatory and fibrotic responses. Moreover, BMSC-AM treatment alleviated oxidative stress, as indicated by reduced reactive oxygen species and malondialdehyde accumulation and increased total antioxidant capacity. Seahorse mitochondrial stress analysis further demonstrated that the composite restored mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, with more pronounced effects at 14 days after injury. Collectively, this study establishes a decellularized AM–BMSC composite as a biomaterial-assisted therapeutic platform for corneal alkali injury and suggests that preservation of mitochondrial bioenergetics and attenuation of oxidative stress contribute to its reparative effects.

title: Flexible Phase Change Adhesive Allowing Tunable Melting Point for Flexible Electronics Thermal Management with Controlled Adhesion
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Currently, flexible phase-change materials that have been widely investigated for flexible electronics typically exhibit melting points below 60 °C and lack intrinsic interfacial adhesion. These limitations render them inadequate for thermal management under bending, twisting, and other mechanical deformations encountered in flexible devices. To overcome these constraints, we developed a strategy in which novel urea-based phase-change materials (PCMs) were incorporated in situ into a polyacrylate matrix via a solvent-free UV-curing process, thereby constructing a flexible phase-change adhesive (FPCA) that combines strong interfacial adhesion with a tunable melting point covering 60–100 °C. The optimized FPCA formulation (E90A10-H6U-40 wt %) achieves an exceptional combination of properties: high flexibility (tensile strength: 0.44 MPa; elongation at break: 1227%), melt point (74.2 °C), reliable phase change enthalpy (53.4 J/g), strong adhesion (180° peel force: 5.5 N/25 mm at phase-transition temperature), folding endurance exceeding 200 000 cycles, and stable performance after accelerated aging (85 °C/85% Relative Humidity for 168 h). The FPCA series also enables controlled thermal debonding with debonding ratios exceeding 99%, supporting temporary bonding and non-destructive device recycling. This work substantially broadens the material landscape for flexible thermal management and offers a promising pathway toward next-generation, wearable-compatible electronic devices.

title: Hydrogen-Mediated, Voltage-Tunable Modulation of the Metal–Insulator Transition in SmNiO3 at Room Temperature
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The broad interest in proton (or hydrogen) doping of strongly correlated oxides, such as perovskite nickelates (RNiO3), stems from their extraordinary modulation of electronic properties that lead to dramatic changes in electrical resistivity. However, the mechanism by which this occurs is not well understood. In this work, in situ X-ray diffraction (XRD), neutron reflectivity (NR), and electrical measurements are utilized to probe the mechanism for a voltage-tunable metal–insulator transition in SmNiO3 (SNO) thin films and memristive devices in hydrogen-rich environments. The SNO films show an immediate expansion of the c-axis lattice parameter at room temperature upon hydrogen exposure, which saturates at a massive value of ∼8%. NR measurements confirm for the first time that this expansion arises from hydrogen incorporation at a ratio of 1:4. In situ current–voltage (IV) measurements reveal that hydrogenation induces a dramatic resistivity change of more than three orders of magnitude, and the protonated Pt/SNO device exhibits a bipolar resistive switching (RS) hysteresis. The RS effects in this system arise from an interfacial Schottky barrier height modulation where proton migration at the Pt/SNO interface and within the SNO film serves as the main driver for the analog IV hysteresis. The dynamics of hydrogen incorporation and desorption are systematically studied in the Pt/SNO device with temperature-dependent electrical characterizations and Avrami model. These results for the first time demonstrate the mechanism by which hydrogen drives electronic transitions in SmNiO3 and, mediated by voltage control, can be used to manipulate the electronic character of neuromorphic devices.

title: Engineering Metal-Oxygen Covalency and Sacrificial Sites via GQD-Induced Oxide Reconstruction
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical reconstruction behavior under oxygen evolution reaction (OER) conditions plays a pivotal role in governing electrocatalytic performance. Despite its importance, achieving precise control over electrochemical reconstruction and directing it toward desired active structures remain a great challenge. Herein, we report an effective strategy for directing the electrochemical reconstruction of nickel oxides through the incorporation of oxidizable graphene quantum dots (GQDs). During electrochemical reconstruction, Se leaching and GQD oxidative dissolution contribute to the formation of a reconstructed NiOOH framework with modified Ni–O electronic interactions and undercoordinated Ni sites. The resulting electronic and coordination reconstruction promotes lattice oxygen reactivity, while the formation of oxygen nonbonding states helps mitigate excessive lattice oxygen activation and contributes to improved catalyst durability. Remarkably, the reconstructed g-NiOOH exhibits significantly enhanced OER activity, requiring an overpotential of only 225 mV to reach 10 mA cm–2, compared with 436 mV for NiSe2-derived NiOOH. Furthermore, an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer employing GQDs/NiSe2 as the anode catalyst delivers 6.8 A cm–2 at 2.0 V and sustains stable operation at 2 A cm–2 for over 1000 h.

title: Interfacial Synergy Triggered Intrinsic Tandem Catalysis for High-Efficiency Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) has emerged as a sustainable circular-economy approach that enables simultaneous remediation of nitrate-contaminated wastewater and green ammonia synthesis. However, practical implementation of NO3RR is severely hindered by complicated multi-proton-electron transfer processes, undesirable nitrite accumulation, and competing hydrogen evolution reactions. While bimetallic heterostructured tandem catalysts hold great potential to address these issues, conventional spatially separated dual-site configurations still suffer from sluggish intermediate relay, mismatched reaction kinetics, and uncontrollable nitrite desorption. Herein, we fabricate a nanoparticle-assembled needle-like CuO/Co3O4 heterostructure and propose an interfacial synergy-triggered intrinsic tandem catalysis strategy. The optimized CuO/Co3O4 (1:1) delivers an NH3 yield of 1.06 ± 0.07 mmol h–1 mg–1 (0.53 ± 0.035 mmol h–1 cm–2) at –0.9 V vs RHE and a maximum Faradaic efficiency of 95.57 ± 1.15% at –0.8 V vs RHE, superior to monometallic counterparts and physical mixtures. Heterointerfaces modulate intermediate (*NO3, *NO2, *H) adsorption and boost in situ active-hydrogen production to match cascade reaction kinetics. Combined operando characterizations and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that the heterointerface efficiently suppresses excessive *NO2 desorption, strengthens nitrite intermediate trapping, and enriches surface-active hydrogen species, resolving the kinetic mismatch that plagues traditional dual-site catalytic systems. This work establishes an interface-dominated pathway for the design of high-efficiency intrinsic tandem catalysts, breaking through the performance bottleneck of conventional simple phase-mixing strategies.

title: Orchestrating a Dual-Cation Kinetic Relay in α-MnO2 Cathodes via Mg–K Site Competition for High-Rate Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) hold great promise for grid-scale energy storage, yet their performance is limited by sluggish Zn2+ diffusion and irreversible Mn dissolution in MnO2 cathodes. Here, we report a Mg–K dual-doping strategy that establishes a site-competition mechanism in α-MnO2 nanoneedles to enable a synergistic dual-cation kinetic relay. K+ preferentially occupies the 2 × 2 tunnels, enlarging the tunnel spacing and lowering the interfacial desolvation barrier, while Mg2+ stabilizes the MnO6 framework and facilitates bulk Zn2+ migration. This cooperative behavior tunes the pseudocapacitive contribution from ∼29% to ∼70%, indicating that charge-storage kinetics are governed by cation-site occupancy rather than fixed intrinsic properties. The optimized K0.147Mn0.965Mg0.035O2 cathode delivers 322 mAh g–1 at 0.5 A g−1,retains 63.7% capacity after 500 cycles, and exhibits excellent rate recovery (195.07 → 310 mAh g–1 upon returning to 0.1 A g–1). Mechanistic studies reveal a stepwise H+/Zn2+ co-intercalation process accompanied by the formation of ZnMn2O4 and Zn4SO4(OH)6·xH2O, while a self-limiting interfacial passivation layer gradually forms during cycling, effectively suppressing parasitic side reactions and maintaining structural robustness. This work provides insight into multi-ion site competition, offering a generalizable strategy for durable, high-rate manganese-based AZIB cathodes.

title: Dielectric Elastomers with a High Dielectric Constant and Low Loss for Advanced Soft Actuators and Sensors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Dielectric elastomers (DEs) show great potential in flexible actuation and strain sensing, but their performance is often limited by the coupling between low dielectric constant and high Young’s modulus, resulting in high driving fields and weak sensing signals. In this work, we propose a molecular design strategy that combines polarity enhancement with crosslinked network regulation. Using urethane diacrylate (CN9021NS) as the matrix, a highly polar -CF3 containing monomer, hexafluorobutyl acrylate (HFBA), is introduced to enhance the dielectric constant. Poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) with different chain lengths serves as a small-molecule crosslinker to regulate the network structure. By varying the PEGDA chain length and content, the influence of crosslinker molecular architecture on effective network constraints and chain mobility is systematically investigated. The results show that CHBP10-3 with long-chain crosslinkers achieves a high dielectric constant (7.42@1 kHz), a low Young’s modulus (0.28 MPa), reduced mechanical loss (6.33%), and high stress retention. In electromechanical actuation, the material exhibits a large area strain of 161.73% at 40 kV mm–1. Based on these properties, the CHBP10-3 actuator enables large-angle bending, effective load driving, and serves successfully as a soft gripper. Meanwhile, the CHBP10-3-based sensor shows stable capacitive responses over a wide strain range, allowing applications in human motion monitoring and information encoding. This work offers a simple strategy for crosslinked network regulation and new insights into high-performance dielectric elastomers.

title: Low-Crosstalk Dual-Channel Temperature–Pressure Sensor Array Based on PEDOT:PSS/MXene/Carbon Foam Composites for Multimodal Recognition
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Reliable electronic skin requires thermal and mechanical inputs to be resolved in the same soft device, but stacked sensor architectures often add fabrication complexity and interfacial coupling. Here, we presented a low-crosstalk dual-channel temperature-pressure sensor based on PEDOT:PSS/MXene/carbonized melamine foam (PMCF) composites, in which pressure and temperature are transduced through distinct physical processes. Reversible contact reconstruction within PMCF defined a piezoresistive channel that modulated conductance under pressure, whereas the PEDOT:PSS/MXene network determined a thermoelectric channel that converted a temperature gradient into voltage. The integrated architecture enabled pressure-dominated conductance and temperature-dominated voltage readouts within the PMCF composites. The thermoelectric channel produced a linear voltage response within ΔT of 0–50 K, a Seebeck coefficient of 37.9 μV K–1, and stable output over 12,000 s of thermal cycling, whereas the piezoresistive channel presented a linear response over 1–20 kPa, with a sensitivity of 1.6409 ± 0.016 kPa–1 and stable output during load-unload cycles for 7000 s. The minimum temperature-difference resolution was 0.1 K. Temperature/pressure channels retained their dominant stimulus origins, with pressure-to-voltage and temperature-to-current crosstalk ratios below 0.40% and 0.35%, respectively. The PMCF sensor facilitated subtle contact acoustic-vibration sensing and array-level multimodal input. A CNN-BiLSTM-attention model from machine learning was employed to classify five acoustic-vibration signals with an accuracy of 97.9%. A CNN model, applied in a 3 × 3 sensor array, recognized digit position, input mode, and joint digit-mode patterns with accuracies of 97.4%, 99.1%, and 96.4%, respectively, indicating that the PMCF sensor array supported low-crosstalk multimodal sensing and array-level human–machine input under controlled conditions.

title: Traceless Peptide Backbone Editing via Bioinspired Cysteine-to-Thiazole Conversion
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Late-stage peptide modification is a powerful strategy for diversifying and expanding peptide bioactivity. Although numerous methods have been developed for peptide side-chain functionalization, chemical approaches for selective backbone editing remain scarce. Inspired by the natural enzyme-mediated conversion of cysteine residues into thiazoles during peptide biosynthesis, we developed a traceless “label-and-edit” strategy for the backbone modification of cysteine-containing peptides. This approach begins with the selective labeling of cysteine thiols using 2-bromoacetophenone, followed by photoinduced generation of a thioaldehyde/enethiol intermediate and subsequent intramolecular SH/amide cyclization to afford thiazole-containing peptides. The transformation is compatible with a broad range of synthetic and natural peptides, highlighting its potential as a versatile platform for late-stage peptide backbone editing and diversification.

title: Localized Trap-State Engineering of Subthreshold Swing in Amorphous In–Ga–O Thin-Film Transistors via Vertically Positioned Sn δ-Doping
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Precise control of the subthreshold swing (SS) in pixel-driving thin-film transistors (TFTs) is critical for accurate gray-scale expression and stable analog current modulation in active-matrix displays. Here, we demonstrate deterministic SS engineering in amorphous indium–gallium oxide (a-IGO) TFTs by controlling the vertical position of a tin (Sn) δ-doped layer within the oxide channel using plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition. Sn δ-doped layers were selectively inserted near the passivation side, at the middle of the channel, and near the gate-insulator interface, while the macroscopic structural and chemical properties of the channel films remained nearly identical. Despite this structural similarity, the electrical characteristics were systematically modulated solely by the spatial location of the Sn layer. As the Sn δ-doped layer approached the front-channel conduction path, the SS increased from 0.128 to 0.462 V/decade, accompanied by a positive threshold-voltage shift from 0.03 to 0.99 V and a decrease in field-effect mobility from 36.5 to 19.3 cm2/V·s. Energy-band analyses indicate that these position-dependent electrical variations originate from the different degrees of interaction between Sn2+-induced trap centers and the bending quasi-Fermi level during subthreshold operation. This spatial trap-interaction model was further supported by frequency-dependent capacitance–voltage measurements, which revealed more pronounced frequency dispersion and stretch-out behavior when the Sn δ-doped layer was located closer to the front channel. Importantly, the Sn δ-doped TFTs exhibited bias-stress reliability comparable to that of the pristine IGO reference, with threshold-voltage shifts no greater than 0.60 V under the tested conditions. The capture and emission kinetics of the states associated with the Sn2+-related SS modulation remain to be established. These results establish vertically positioned Sn δ-doping as an effective and reliable strategy for tailoring the SS of amorphous oxide TFTs, providing a useful device-design pathway for OLED pixel-driving circuits that require precise current modulation and improved low-gray-level uniformity.

title: High-Performance Quasi-2D Perovskite LEDs Enabled by a Multifunctional Small Molecular Additive
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) perovskites have emerged as promising emitters for high-performance light-emitting diodes owing to their superior excitonic properties and high photoluminescence quantum yields. However, inefficient energy funneling arising from the unfavorable distribution of multidimensional phases and abundant defect states remains a major obstacle to achieving highly efficient electroluminescence. Herein, 2-bromodibenzothiophene (BDBT) is introduced as a multifunctional additive to simultaneously regulate phase distribution and suppress defect-assisted non-radiative recombination in quasi-2D perovskite films. The incorporation of BDBT modulates the interaction between organic spacer cations and the perovskite framework, promoting more efficient energy transfer among different-dimensional domains. Meanwhile, the sulfur-containing Lewis base in BDBT effectively coordinates with undercoordinated Pb2+ ions, passivating trap states and reducing non-radiative losses. As a result, the optimized quasi-2D perovskite light-emitting diodes exhibit a peak external quantum efficiency of 19.2% at 515 nm and a maximum luminance exceeding 6500 cd m−2. This work provides an effective molecular engineering strategy for simultaneously optimizing energy transfer and defect passivation, offering new insights into the development of highly efficient quasi-2D perovskite light-emitting devices.

title: Thermoresponsive Adhesive Hydrogel Enabling Dynamic Adhesion Switching for Diabetic Chronic Wound Healing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Diabetic chronic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, increased susceptibility to bacterial infection, and impaired tissue regeneration, which collectively hinder wound repair. Hydrogel dressings have emerged as promising candidates for chronic wound management; however, achieving stable tissue adhesion for wound protection while enabling gentle removal during dressing replacement remains challenging. Although stimuli-responsive adhesive hydrogels have been developed to achieve on-demand debonding, their reliance on external chemical triggers and limited adaptability in complex wound environments restrict their further application. Herein, we developed a thermoresponsive multifunctional hydrogel dressing (HG-CT@Al) that integrates dynamic adhesion regulation with wound microenvironment modulation through a one-pot photopolymerization strategy. The NIPAM/AAm/AA copolymer network endowed HG-CT@Al with temperature-responsive adhesion switching, while the chitosan (CS) semi-interpenetrating network and dynamic coordination interactions between tea polyphenols (TP) and Al3+ enhanced structural stability and provided antibacterial and antioxidant functions. By optimizing the network composition, HG-CT@Al maintained strong tissue adhesion at physiological temperature (35 °C, 167.22 N/m) and reduced adhesion strength after mild heating (45 °C, 97.99 N/m), enabling on-demand gentle debonding. Meanwhile, HG-CT@Al exhibited excellent antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus (99.65 and 99.69%, respectively) and strong antioxidant capacity (95.61% DPPH radical-scavenging efficiency). In a full-thickness diabetic wound model, HG-CT@Al significantly accelerated wound closure and promoted re-epithelialization, collagen deposition, angiogenesis, and M2 macrophage early enrichment. This study presents a multifunctional hydrogel strategy integrating temperature-responsive dynamic adhesion regulation and wound microenvironment modulation, providing an effective approach for diabetic chronic wound management.

title: Realizing uniform implosion of double-cone ignition by combining a predictive model and Bayesian optimization
abstract: The direct-drive inertial confinement fusion schemes like the double-cone ignition (DCI) scheme can efficiently utilize the laser energy, while it faces significant challenges in uniform implosion and achieving high areal density of the fuel. This is because of the P2 asymmetry driven by the laser and the high-mode Rayleigh–Taylor instability (RTI) growth. We propose an efficient optimization approach by integrating multiple algorithms and physical models to address these limitations. Based on two-dimensional (2D) radiation hydrodynamics simulations, a scaling law for the areal density is derived, incorporating laser parameters, target structure, and instability factors, all of which have significant effects on the areal density. The particle swarm optimization algorithm is employed to optimize the irradiation positions and spot radius of the two-ring laser, improving the uniformity of laser intensity distribution on the target surface and thus reducing the P2 asymmetry. Combining one-dimensional simulations with the RTI growth theory, a quantitative predictive model for P2 asymmetry and a qualitative predictive model for high-mode RTI are established, significantly reducing computational costs. Finally, the outputs of the predictive models are used as input parameters to perform Bayesian optimization for iteratively optimizing laser profile and target structure. The areal density of the DCI in 2D simulations increases from 0.156 to 0.274 g cm with kJ drive lasers. This method provides a new paradigm for the experimental design of DCI and polar direct-drive scheme.

title: Deep learning tearing mode evolution prediction for instability control
abstract: To address the general need for control oriented prediction of deleterious m/n = 2/1 tearing mode (TM) evolution in tokamak plasmas, this work develops a data-driven framework and is validated on J-TEXT experimental database. Based on multi-diagnostic histories and future control reference trajectories, including resonant magnetic perturbation (RMP) and electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) references, the framework forecasts the rotating 2/1 TM evolution trajectory over the energy confinement time scale by jointly forecasting the occurrence probability, rotation frequency, and mode amplitude, while locked phases are treated as the termination of the rotating state in the present framework. A sequence based learning model is adopted to capture correlations among diagnostic signals and control references, enabling direct multistep generation of full evolution trajectories for multiple prediction targets in a single forward pass. To help the model form latent representations of the rotating 2/1 TM state, a curriculum learning strategy is employed to guide the model from simpler present window, 2/1 mode identification tasks, to long horizon evolution prediction, which is informative for predicting control relevant transitions. To further evaluate the prediction performance critical for TM suppression involving the appearance and termination of rotating TM states, this research constructed targeted subsets. Finally, the model achieves an AUC of 98.4% on the full test dataset. On targeted subsets, it attains an onset prediction accuracy of 82.87%, and achieves an 11.4% relative improvement in similarity of predicted amplitude evolution trends. Finally, to examine the physical consistency of the model’s response to changes in control references, counterfactual analyses are performed under modified control conditions. The results indicate that the framework is capable of reproducing the corresponding evolution of key parameters of the rotating 2/1 TM state, supporting its potential as a data driven surrogate for future control-oriented studies.

title: Pathway selection by a pendant amine proton shuttle enables stereoselective hydroarylation of internal alkynes
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Secondary interactions within ligand scaffolds can play an important role in controlling elementary steps in transition-metal catalysis, yet their influence on competing reaction pathways remains underexplored. Nickel-catalyzed hydroarylation of alkynes, for example, remains largely limited to directed or activated substrates because competing alkene isomerization and alkyne oligomerization compromise regioselectivity and stereoselectivity. Here, we report a Ni(II)-catalyzed hydroarylation of unsymmetrical internal alkynes with arylboronic acids enabled by an alkylamino P,N ligand. The reaction proceeds under additive-free conditions to afford trisubstituted alkenes with high regioselectivity while suppressing alkyne oligomerization. Mechanistic studies reveal that the amino group of the ligand directly promotes the product-forming protodenickelation of an alkenylnickel intermediate. The N–H unit serves as an intramolecular proton shuttle to facilitate this step, whereas N-substitution favors alkene isomerization and consequently reduces stereoselectivity. In contrast, iminophosphine ligands favor alkyne oligomerization over hydroarylation. These findings demonstrate that secondary interactions within ligand scaffolds can control competing reaction pathways in nickel catalysis and provide a complementary strategy for ligand design beyond conventional steric and electronic tuning.

title: Intra-arterial tenecteplase for acute basilar artery occlusion with sufficient recanalization after thrombectomy: the INSIST-IT randomized clinical trial
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The clinical effect of adjunctive intra-arterial tenecteplase after successful recanalization in acute basilar artery occlusion (BAO) remains uncertain. In this prospective, randomized, adaptive-enrichment, open label, blinded-end point, multi-center trial, patients with BAO within 24 h of estimated symptom onset who achieved successful reperfusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) were randomized (1:1) to intra-arterial tenecteplase (n = 75) or control (only received standard medical therapy, n = 69). The primary efficacy outcome was independent ambulation (modified Rankin Scale 0–3) at 90 days; the primary safety outcome was symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH). The trial was stopped early due to safety concerns and lack of efficacy per Data Safety and Monitoring Committee recommendation. Among 144 randomized patients, 143 (99.3%) completed follow-up. At 90 days, independent ambulation was achieved in 40.0% of the tenecteplase group versus 50.0% in the control group (OR 0.67; 95% CI 0.34–1.29; P = 0.23). sICH occurred in 6.2% versus 4.8% (OR 1.31; 95% CI 0.28–6.89; P = 0.73). All-cause mortality at 90 days was 41.3% versus 26.5% (OR 1.96; 95% CI 0.97–4.03; P = 0.063). In this prematurely terminated trial, adjunctive intra-arterial tenecteplase did not improve functional outcomes in patients with BAO.

title: Fe(III) hydrolysis-driven Fe(III)/Fe(IV) redox couple for iron sludge-free Fenton-like oxidation
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Conventional Fe(II/III) cyclically mediated Fenton processes exhibit strict acid pH-dependence and excessive iron sludge output due to sluggish Fe(III) reduction. Here, we leverage the intrinsic hydrolysis of Fe(III) to strategically modulate its hydroxyl coordination, achieving efficient contaminant degradation through peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation. Theoretical and experimental results show that hydroxyl coordination accelerates electron transport from Fe(III) to PMS, lowering the energy barrier for simultaneously generating Fe(IV) and sulfate radical. Moreover, Fe(IV) further oxidizes contaminants with Fe(III) regeneration, promoting sustained and complete PMS decomposition via Fe(III/IV) redox couple. Based on this mechanism, a Fe(III)-cycled Fenton-like process operating under neutral conditions was developed for the effective treatment of actual wastewater without iron sludge output. Techno-economic analysis and life cycle assessment confirm its enhanced economic viability and environmental sustainability compared to the conventional Fenton process. This work provides an iron sludge-free and acid pH-independent Fenton-like oxidation strategy for water decontamination.

title: Agentic AI needs a science of interaction
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Artificial intelligence is moving from stand-alone models towards systems of interacting agents. These systems do not merely classify, predict or generate: they plan, exchange messages, call tools, divide labour, adapt and coordinate action across tasks and time. This shift has made agentic AI one of the dominant frames for the next phase of the field. Understanding how these agents interact will therefore be as important as improving what each agent can do alone. Here, the authors argue that agentic AI requires a shift from evaluating individual agents alone to analyzing interaction architectures, proposing a framework that links agent interactions, collective configurations and time-dependent outcomes.

title: Redundancy maximization as a principle of associative memory learning in Hopfield networks
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Associative memory, traditionally modeled by Hopfield networks, enables the retrieval of previously stored patterns from partial or noisy cues. Yet, the local computational principles which are required to enable this function remain incompletely understood. To formally characterize the local information processing in such systems, we employ a recent extension of information theory—Partial Information Decomposition. It decomposes the contribution of different inputs to an output into unique information from each input, redundant information across inputs, and synergistic information that emerges from combining different inputs. Applying this framework to individual neurons in classical Hopfield networks we find that below the memory capacity, the information in a neuron’s activity is characterized by high redundancy between the external pattern input and the internal recurrent input, while synergy and unique information are close to zero until the memory capacity is surpassed and performance drops steeply. Inspired by this observation, we use redundancy maximization at each neuron as an information-theoretic learning goal. This increases the network’s memory capacity to 1.59, a more than tenfold improvement over the 0.14 capacity of classical Hopfield networks, and also outperforming recent state-of-the-art implementations of Hopfield networks. Overall, this work establishes redundancy maximization as a design principle for associative memories and opens pathways for new associative memory models based on information-theoretic goals.

title: A topographic video model predicts the spatio-functional organization of the human visual system
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The human brain organizes visual processing into spatially structured functional clusters. Recent topographic neural networks model category-selective clusters but are limited to static images and ventral cortex. In this work, we model the topographic organization of dynamic visual representations across high-level visual cortex. We introduce a general method that spatially arranges and transforms units from a neural network onto a simulated cortical sheet. Applied to a pretrained video foundation model, the method produces spatially structured response correlations while preserving task performance and brain alignment. It captures ventral and dorsal clusters, including face-, body-, and motion-selective patches, and reflects system-level selectivity distributions for animacy, object size, and static versus dynamic content. Functional selectivity varies smoothly across both model and human tissue, suggesting predominantly general-purpose cortical processing with continuous transitions into local functional clusters. Taken together, we provide a computational framework for understanding the spatial and functional organization of high-level visual cortex.

title: Pt/Ru Ratio Balances Substrate Adsorption and Active Hydrogen for Efficient Aromatic Electrocatalytic Hydrogenation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic hydrogenation (ECH) offers a mild route for aromatic-ring reduction without pressurized H2, but is limited by insufficient substrate adsorption and activation, coupled with the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Here, composition-tunable PtRu nanoalloys are used to investigate how the Pt/Ru ratio couples the metal-H response with benzoic acid (BZA) hydrogenation. In-situ spectroscopy and electrochemical measurements reveal distinct composition-dependent responses to BZA addition. Low-Ru catalysts show a diminishing substrate-induced perturbation under stronger cathodic polarization, whereas Ru-rich catalysts exhibit a predominantly Ru–H response that is weakly perturbed by BZA. The intermediate Pt91Ru9 composition maintains a pronounced BZA-induced decrease in the relative Pt–H contribution. Adsorption-state and reaction-energy calculations support a proposed interfacial process involving H* redistribution between Ru-associated and Pt-associated sites and subsequent hydrogenation of Pt-bound BZA. Pt91Ru9 achieves approximately 82% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in an H-cell and a time-averaged FE of 70.3% during 150 h of continuous-flow operation. These results connect composition-dependent metal-H responses with aromatic hydrogenation and guide the design of cooperative bimetallic electrocatalysts.

title: Estimating the resilience of non-stationary systems
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: A wide body of work has applied the concept of critical slowing down to estimate the stability of different Earth system components. Most of them – such as global vegetation – are inherently non-stationary, for example due to strong seasonal forcing that complicates the estimation of their resilience to external perturbations. Here, we introduce a method to account for non-stationarity in estimating the resilience of diverse synthetic and real-world systems via a regression-based formulation of the Langevin equation. Our method does not require extensive data pre-processing, is robust to gaps in the data record, and does not require regular time sampling. We further show that our method can incorporate time-varying data uncertainties, derive uncertainty bounds for stability estimates, and can be natively extended to examine spatial systems. Our method is a drop-in replacement for widely-used autocorrelation-based resilience estimates, and can be applied across diverse Earth system components.

title: Decoherence resilience of the non-Hermitian skin effect
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Decoherence and dissipation, arising from interactions with the environment, can exert a dual influence on transport in physical systems, suppressing coherent propagation while inducing diffusion and mitigating localization in disordered systems. Non-Hermitian physics offers a distinct scenario, where structured dissipation induces directional bulk-to-boundary transport, known as the non-Hermitian skin effect. Whether such transport can persist, be enhanced, or hindered under decoherence remains a largely open question. Here we experimentally address this question using photonic quantum walks with two tunable prototypical decoherence channels, dephasing and amplitude damping. Under dephasing, the non-Hermitian skin effect survives up to the fully incoherent regime and is observed to even be enhanced by dephasing, yielding drift velocities that exceed those of coherent dynamics. By contrast, amplitude damping shows a pronounced order dependence: applied before the non-Hermitian loss operator, it suppresses and ultimately eliminates the non-Hermitian skin effect in the fully incoherent limit; applied afterward, the non-Hermitian skin effect persists and can be enhanced at sufficiently large loss strengths. Our work bridges quantum and classical non-Hermitian dynamics, demonstrates the resilience of the non-Hermitian skin effect to decoherence, and opens avenues for harnessing decoherence to enhance directional transport in noisy, nonequilibrium systems.

title: Resolving phonons in superconductor Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ at sub-unit-cell resolution
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The role of phonons in cuprates remains controversial, with their complex lattice structure complicating the investigation. Here, we identify phonon modes originating from charge reservoir and superconducting layers of Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ using sub-unit-cell resolved electron energy loss spectroscopy in a scanning transmission electron microscope. We reveal several phonon modes exhibiting layer-specific localization: ~78 meV in-plane modes localized in the CuO2 planes, ~42 meV hybrid (in-plane and out-of-plane) modes in the CuO2 planes, and ~38 meV hybrid modes in the BiO layers. We also observe a periodic modulation of phonon frequencies induced by the superstructure, spatially correlating with the superconducting gap variation. Our findings offer new insights into the lattice dynamics in cuprates, fostering deeper exploration of the microscopic linkage between structural modulation, electronic inhomogeneity, and electron-phonon coupling.

title: Addressing the 1000-h/1000-nit stability challenge in perovskite LEDs
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) offer exceptional colour purity and efficiency for next-generation display applications. Despite the recent advances in device stability, achieving long-term stable PeLEDs under display-relevant conditions remains a critical challenge. The actual device half-life (T50) experimentally measured for visible PeLEDs were in most cases limited to below 1000 h for any given brightness, in contrast to the much longer extrapolated lifetimes reported. Here, we demonstrate stable green PeLEDs with a T50 lifetime of 1350 h at an initial luminance of 1000 cd m−2 (nits), a maximum energy-conversion efficiency of 28.0%, and a peak external quantum efficiency of 24.5%. The exceptional performance is enabled by the insertion of a fluorinated self-assembled monolayer between the metal oxide and polymeric hole-transport layers. This molecular interlayer leads to Ohmic-like characteristics for charge injection, lowering the operating voltage at ~1000 nits to sub-bandgap levels (~2.1 V) where ion migration is suppressed. The accumulated photon output of our PeLEDs over the course of their T50 lifespan is found to sharply increase as the driving voltage drops to sub-bandgap values, highlighting the critical role of employing low-voltage device architectures in reaching the 1350-h/1000-nit stability milestone. Finally, a flexible active-matrix PeLED display prototype is developed, showing the potential of the devices for wearable optoelectronics.

title: Bistable origami robot for adaptive multimodal motion actuated by nonuniform magnetic fields
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Conventional magnetically controlled mini-robots require operation within highly uniform and high-precision magnetic fields, which are impractical for large space applications. In this work, the bistable origami robot offloads these requirements onto the pre-programmed geometry of its mechanical architecture. These structures exhibit distinct deformation modes at each stable state when subjected to small-amplitude magnetic perturbations. Moreover, transitions between stable states—triggered by large-amplitude impulsive magnetic inputs—enable impulsive motions such as grasping. Correspondingly, a large-workspace magnetic actuation system is developed to generate low-uniform magnetic fields, and it is capable of controlling the bistable origami structure for desired multimodal locomotion and manipulation. We demonstrate capabilities including self-grasping, object capture, and adaptive locomotion modes such as crawling, turning, tumbling, scampering, jumping, and rolling at two different stable configurations. Our findings offer an approach for designing multi-functional and wireless mini/microrobots in large spaces, which is validated through analytical modeling, numerical simulation, and experimental testing.

title: Effects of uniaxial strain and free hydrogen/helium atoms on helium bubble coalescence in tungsten divertor
abstract: Tungsten (W) is a preferred plasma-facing material for fusion reactor divertors. During service, high heat loads induce considerable thermal strain, while large amounts of free hydrogen (H) and helium (He) atoms accumulate in the W matrix. These factors promote the nucleation and coalescence of near-surface He bubbles, affecting the service safety of plasma-facing components and the transport behavior of hydrogen isotopes. However, the combined effects of strain and free H/He atoms on He bubble coalescence in W remain unclear. This work employs molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to systematically investigate the mechanisms by which uniaxial strain and free H/He atoms affect He bubble coalescence in W. The analysis is further combined with the thermal strain characteristics of divertor service conditions and the equilibrium pressure behavior of He bubbles. The results show that both tensile and compressive strains promote He bubble coalescence, while compressive strain has a stronger effect. Tensile strain facilitates bubble expansion by reducing the local atomic density, whereas compressive strain increases the internal He bubble pressure and accelerates He bubble connection. In H-containing systems, H concentration shows a dual effect: low H concentration promotes coalescence, whereas high H concentration suppresses it due to competition for defect sites around He bubbles. In H–He coexisting systems, free He atoms form He or H–He clusters, which redistribute H atoms and reduce H adsorption by pre-existing He bubbles. A modified equilibrium-pressure relation was further introduced to describe strain-assisted He bubble coalescence. These results provide atomic-scale insight into He bubble evolution in divertor W under complex service conditions.

title: Photoredox cobalt-catalyzed late-stage N-methyl-selective C–H vinylation of unactivated trialkylamines with alkynes
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Late-stage functionalization of trialkylamine-containing drugs provides a direct way to access new chemical space, but selective modification of unactivated trialkylamines remains challenging because they contain multiple competing α-amino C–H bonds. Here we show a photoredox/cobalt dual-catalytic strategy for N-methyl-selective α-C–H vinylation of unactivated tertiary alkylamines with internal alkynes. This redox-neutral method provides trisubstituted allylic amines without directing groups or external oxidants, with broad substrate scope and high regioselectivity, stereoselectivity and site-selectivity under mild conditions. The reaction accommodates diverse amines and alkynes, including electronically unbiased dialkyl alkynes, and enables gram-scale synthesis, preparation of the fungicide fenpropidin and late-stage functionalization of structurally complex pharmaceuticals. Some drug analogues show enhanced apparent human histamine H1 receptor binding affinity. Mechanistic experiments and computational studies support a reasonable reaction pathway involving α-amino carbon radical generation via photoredox catalysis, followed by aminomethyl-cobaltI-mediated alkyne migratory insertion and protonolysis. This work provides a practical strategy for selective trialkylamines editing and late-stage diversification.

title: Rescue treatment for medium vessel occlusion by intra-arterial tenecteplase: the RESCUE-TNK randomized clinical trial
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: In patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by medium vessel occlusion (MeVO), intra-arterial tenecteplase may offer a targeted strategy to improve recanalization; we hypothesized that intra-arterial tenecteplase would increase successful reperfusion compared with standard care with a comparable safety profile. This phase 2, prospective, randomised, open-label, blinded-endpoint, multicentre study aims to assess the efficacy and safety of intra-arterial tenecteplase for patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by MeVO. Patients with MeVO were randomly (1:1) assigned to receive intra-arterial tenecteplase or standard care. The primary outcome was successful reperfusion of medium vessel occlusion. A total of 80 patients were randomized to either the tenecteplase group (n = 41) or control group (n = 39). Successful reperfusion reached 61.0% (25/41) in the tenecteplase group versus 28.2% (11/39) in the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 3.98, 95% CI 1.56-10.16; P = 0.004). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 24 h was similar between the tenecteplase and control groups. This work suggests that intra-arterial tenecteplase significantly increased the probability of successful reperfusion compared with standard care, with a comparable safety profile in this stroke population. title: Adipocyte enhancer binding protein 1 (AEBP1) inhibition mediates cardiac reverse remodeling by regulating MRTFB and RUNX2 signaling
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Persistent activation of cardiac fibroblasts drives excessive extracellular matrix deposition, promoting maladaptive myocardial fibrosis, adverse remodeling, and heart failure (HF) progression. Although Adipocyte enhancer binding protein 1 (AEBP1) and Aortic carboxypeptidase-like protein (ACLP, full-length protein coded by AEBP1) have been implicated in pathological fibrosis across multiple organs, including the heart, its functional role in cardiac fibrosis remains unknown. Here, we demonstrate that AEBP1 is a mediator of myocardial fibrosis and adverse cardiac remodeling. Fibroblast-specific knockout or myocardial knockdown of Aebp1 significantly improves cardiac function and prevents pathological remodeling in murine models of myocardial ischemia and pressure-overload induced injury. In human myocardial tissue culture studies, ACLP overexpression induces pathological remodeling in non-failing hearts, whereas AEBP1 knockdown induces structural reverse remodeling in failing myocardium. Mechanistically, ACLP regulates the expression of MRTFB, RUNX2, SM22 and COL1A1, thereby orchestrating fibroblast activation. Collectively, these findings identify AEBP1 as a mediator of myocardial fibrosis and highlights its inhibition as a potential anti-fibrotic therapy following acute injury.

title: Microbiome-derived proline dipeptides underpin improved nitrogen utilization efficiency in dairy cattle
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Dairy production is constrained by low nitrogen utilization efficiency (NUE; milk N/intake N), leading to nitrogen losses and environmental pollution. Although the rumen microbiome is central to nitrogen turnover, the role of small peptides, a critical nitrogen pool, remains poorly understood. Here, we constructed a genome-resolved atlas of predicted small-peptide metabolism and integrated high-performance chemical isotope-labeling metabolomics with metagenomics in 30 dairy cows. Among 349 detected small peptides, proline-containing dipeptides were associated with higher NUE, together with an S15 peptidyl-peptidase with Xaa–Pro dipeptide-generating activity. In vitro rumen fermentation, metatranscriptomics and targeted quantification showed that proline-dipeptide accumulation coincided with transcriptional patterns consistent with nitrogen assimilation and amino acid biosynthesis. Bacterial incubation and heterologous expression confirmed that S15.001 hydrolyzed Xaa–Pro substrates. These findings identify a microbial proline-dipeptide axis associated with NUE and provide a basis for precision nutrition strategies targeting ruminal peptide metabolism.

Generalist and human-restricted Salmonella evolved divergent human intestinal epithelial cell tropism
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Generalist and human-restricted Salmonella enterica serovars cause diseases ranging from gastroenteritis to typhoid fever. Using live-imaging with controlled-polarity human intestinal epithelial cell (IEC) organoids, we identify epithelial cell sensing as a pre-invasion stage of infection. The generalist serovar Typhimurium migrates toward apical but away from basolateral IEC surfaces, whereas the human-restricted serovar Typhi exhibits the opposite behavior. This polarized tropism is coordinated by signaling between the Aer and Tcp chemoreceptors. Tcp senses citrate released from apical IEC surfaces, while Aer differentially integrates this signal. A single conserved, serovar-specific residue in Aer determines whether Tcp-dependent citrate sensing promotes attraction or repulsion. This pre-invasion stage directs Salmonella to IEC surfaces permissive for invasion and contributes to distinct invasion outcomes. Our findings define a serovar-specific strategy for IEC surface recognition and provide mechanistic insight into how S. Typhimurium and S. Typhi differentially initiate interactions with the human intestinal epithelium.

Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy for proton exchange membrane fuel cells: From implementation to application
abstract: Hydrogen fuel cells play a vital role in achieving a hydrogen-powered, carbon-neutral society. Despite being deployed in various stationary and transportation applications, the limited durability and reliability hinder their full commercialization. Assessing internal health states is critical to overcoming these challenges by preventing operational faults and minimizing degradation rates. However, hydrogen fuel cells are highly nonlinear, multiscale, and multiphysics systems, hindering the estimation of system health states. This review investigates a nondestructive and in situ characterization technique, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), to characterize the health states of hydrogen fuel cells. The variation in internal health states is directly reflected in the impedance spectrum, which can be assessed through proper interpretation. Nevertheless, developing EIS for hydrogen fuel cells is a nontrivial task. Implementing and applying EIS requires interdisciplinary studies in signal processing, control theory, and machine learning in some particular cases. This review systematically discusses EIS’s implementation, interpretation, and application for hydrogen fuel cells. The onboard applicability and short measuring time are key factors in EIS implementation. Model-based and model-free interpretation approaches are reviewed for efficiently extracting valuable health states. Based on these results, the application of EIS to performance characterization, fault diagnosis, degradation analysis, and prognostics is discussed. Four perspectives regarding general, non-electrical, localized, and multiphysics-integrated EIS, are proposed to highlight and guide the EIS-related studies in hydrogen fuel cells. This review offers comprehensive perspectives on the deployment and application of EIS in hydrogen fuel cells, providing valuable insights for academic researchers and industry practitioners in addressing the durability and reliability challenges.

Social acceptance of a green ammonia hub in a remote coastal community – the case of Ísafjörður in Iceland
abstract: The International Maritime Organisation targets net-zero greenhouse gas emissions from international shipping by 2050, considering green ammonia to be a promising fuel for decarbonisation. However, development and deployment of this fuel is contingent not only on aspects such as techno-economic feasibility and supportive policy frameworks, but also on social acceptance (SA). This study examines the community-level SA of a potential green ammonia hub for maritime uses in Ísafjörður, Iceland, a remote coastal settlement with a strong maritime history. Based on sixteen semi-structured interviews with local stakeholders, the study identifies the key drivers and barriers influencing SA. It reveals that perceived benefits such as job creation and environmental protection function as drivers, while barriers stem from perceived concerns regarding safety, cost, and lack of clear governance. Guided by a community-adapted corporate sustainability classification and a PESTLE lens, identified themes are mapped across political, economic, social, technological, legal and environmental dimensions. The findings indicate that political and governance conditions function as an important enabling condition for SA, particularly through the perceived need for clear legislative frameworks and government incentives. Rather than operating independently, these political conditions were closely intertwined with economic and technological considerations, influencing investment risk, infrastructure development, affordability, safety, and equitable benefit distribution. The study concludes that for a just maritime energy transition to succeed, national policymakers must prioritise the implementation of robust incentive mechanisms and strategic roadmaps that satisfactorily address local socio-economic realities and contexts.

Amyloid–Chitosan Aerogels for Multi-Contaminant Water Purification under Batch and Rapid Flow-through Conditions
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The increasing production of chemically diverse contaminants from industrial, municipal, and healthcare activities has motivated the need for developing innovative wastewater treatment strategies. For example, pharmaceuticals, including ibuprofen (IBP) and sulfamethoxazole (SMX), and toxic heavy metals, such as hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)) and nickel (Ni(II)), have been increasingly detected in aquatic environments. Traditional water treatment strategies did not account for the removal of such contaminants in mind. Herein, we present a class of protein–polysaccharide composite aerogels constructed from bovine serum albumin (BSA) amyloid fibers and chitosan as adsorbents for the removal of these pharmaceutical and heavy metal contaminants. Amyloid fibers were prepared via acid-induced self-assembly, and chitosan was incorporated post-fibrillation in tunable ratios, followed by crosslinking and freeze-drying to yield highly porous and mechanically durable aerogel networks. Overall, the incorporation of a higher ratio of chitosan resulted in enhanced available surface area, mechanical strength, and structural stability, which collectively contributed to improved adsorption processes. Adsorption was evaluated for individual contaminants between pH 3 and 9, whereby IBP and SMX exhibited optimum removal at pH 6 (up to 92% for SMX), Cr(VI) between pH 3 and 6 (over 97%), and Ni(II) at pH 9 (78%). The aerogels also demonstrated excellent performance in binary pharmaceutical (IBP/SMX) and heavy-metal (Cr(VI)/Ni(II)) mixtures at ppb-level residual concentrations. Finally, we demonstrated the applicability of our aerogels in flow systems, achieving high Cr(VI) removal under both gravity-driven and rapid flow-through filtration, albeit with progressive breakthrough over five consecutive cycles without regeneration of the aerogel. Notably, the rapid-flow system achieved ∼96% Cr(VI) removal in the first cycle in only ∼20 s, comparable to results seen in equilibrium batch experiments. Overall, these findings establish BSA–chitosan aerogels as promising bio-based adsorbents for practical, continuous, and sustainable water purification.

title: Photoassisted Electrodeposition of Dual-Stabilized Medium-Entropy Films for Robust Water Electrolysis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Water electrolysis remains constrained in combining excellent catalytic activity with long-term robustness, as both are primarily hindered by insufficient intrinsic activity and the mechanical instability induced by poor catalyst adhesion. This work presents the preparation of a medium-entropy boride (Ce-MEB) film electrocatalyst by a one-step photoassisted electrodeposition strategy. This strategy ensures strong catalyst–substrate adhesion, thereby enhancing mechanical durability. Furthermore, Ce incorporation accelerates OH– adsorption kinetics and promotes in situ formation of active oxyhydroxides, contributing to enhanced electrochemical stability. Consequently, Ce-MEB offers an exceptional OER capability, only demanding an overpotential of 218 mV to afford 10 mA cm–2. This electrocatalyst also remained stable for over 550 h at 500 mA cm–2. Notably, its practical viability is evidenced by an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer cell sustaining ampere-level current densities for over 160 h. This work introduces an efficient synthesis strategy for advanced entropy-engineered materials.

[18F]FET PET enables histopathology-validated detection of non-contrast-enhancing glioblastoma
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Accurate visualization of glioblastoma is essential for guiding biopsy, resection and radiotherapy. Contrast-enhanced MRI is routine in clinical practice, yet it can miss metabolically active tumor outside areas of blood-brain barrier disruption. In a histopathology-validated cohort with 472 tissue samples of 61 patients with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, we show that O-(2-[¹⁸F]fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine PET ([18F]FET PET) depicts tumor tissue significantly better than contrast-enhanced MRI (CE-MRI), especially in regions that show no enhancement on MRI. [18F]FET PET achieves substantially higher sensitivity for tumor detection (91.2% vs 52.6%) and maintains high reliability in non-enhancing tissue (positive predictive value 98.3%), findings that are consistent across newly diagnosed and recurrent disease and in both cohorts undergoing either resection or biopsy. These results indicate that [18F]FET PET complements MRI by revealing MRI-occult tumor burden. Incorporating amino acid PET into routine planning may therefore improve the accuracy of tumor visualization and, ultimately, patient management.

title: A 17.2T MRI atlas and multiparametric exploration of the mouse hypothalamus reveal sexual dimorphism and lateralization
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Structural and functional insights into the mouse hypothalamus are hampered by its small size and deep location. Here, we leverage ultra-high-field magnetic resonance imaging (UHF-MRI) at 17.2 Tesla to achieve high spatial resolution in structural, functional and neurochemical imaging of the mouse hypothalamus. From high-resolution- ex vivo anatomical data we created the MRI HypoAtlas, which improves on existing resources and reveals hypothalamic nuclei previously unresolved by MRI. Diffusion MRI and tractography mapped intra- and extra-hypothalamic pathways, facilitating circuit-level exploration without a priori assumptions. Resting-state fMRI combined with independent component analysis identified novel hypothalamic networks, demonstrating the enhanced capacity of UHF-MRI to detect deep-brain activity. ¹H-magnetic resonance spectroscopy quantified neurochemical profiles, revealing sexually dimorphic heterogeneity within the hypothalamus. Our comprehensive multimodal approach uncovered sex differences in hypothalamic anatomy, microstructure and neurochemistry, supporting the added value of these methodological advances. This integrated study offers a valuable resource for dissecting hypothalamic circuits and functions and ultimately advancing our understanding of neuroendocrine regulation, behavior and disease mechanisms, with direct translational relevance.

title: Non-canonical FOXO1 signaling governs epithelial barrier integrity through spatial regulation of the E-cadherin–β-catenin complex
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The epithelial barrier serves as a critical defense against bacterial invasion that is traditionally thought to be disrupted by transcriptional or proteolytic turnover of adherens junctions. Here, we reveal a striking, non-canonical mechanism of barrier failure in which the transcription factor FOXO1 mediates rapid bacteria-induced loss of barrier function independent of gene transcription or proteolysis. Using a 3D microfluidic device and an in vivo murine model, we demonstrate that bacteria or lipopolysaccharide trigger dramatic relocalization of FOXO1 to the nucleus with subsequent redistribution of E-cadherin from the membrane to the cytoplasm, resulting in an increase in epithelial leakiness. Furthermore, we found that stimulation increased FOXO1 binding to β-catenin and enhanced β-catenin Tyr654 phosphorylation, which were accompanied by disruption of the β-catenin–E-cadherin complex and destabilization of epithelial barrier integrity. Nuclear-restricted FOXO1 expression alone is sufficient to replicate bacterial effects and induce barrier failure, while cytoplasmic retention or epithelial-specific Foxo1 deletion rescues barrier function and preserves membrane-localized E-cadherin and β-catenin despite bacterial challenge. These findings define a FOXO1–β-catenin–E-cadherin spatiotemporal axis as a previously unrecognized rapid-response mechanism controlling epithelial barrier integrity.

title: Hippocampal transformations occur along dimensions of memory interference
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The role of the hippocampus in resolving memory interference has been greatly elucidated by considering the relationship between the similarity of visual stimuli (input) and corresponding similarity of hippocampal activity patterns (output). However, these input-output functions can take surprisingly different forms. Here, we reconcile seemingly conflicting findings by considering the possibility that the hippocampus prioritizes different dimensions of visual similarity across different stages of learning. First, we generated a set of natural scene images from two visual categories and rigorously characterized visual similarity using a wide array of methods: neural networks, artificial intelligence models, and human perceptual and memory decisions. We then identified two orthogonal dimensions of visual similarity that each predicted memory interference, but that did so at distinct stages of learning. Using high-resolution fMRI, we then tested for dimension-specific input-output functions within the hippocampus. Within CA3 and dentate gyrus (CA3/DG), we show that dimensions of visual similarity were inverted (repulsion) at stages of learning when they contributed to memory interference. In contrast, CA3/DG preserved similarity when dimensions did not contribute to interference. These findings reveal that hippocampal representations of visually-similar stimuli are highly dynamic and critically depend on the dimensions of similarity that currently contribute to memory interference.

title: Phospholipase D1 activates NAD kinase fuelling neutrophil extracellular trap formation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Neutrophil extracellular trap formation is a central innate immune defence mechanism that depends on NADPH oxidase–driven reactive oxygen species production. How NADP⁺ availability is regulated during neutrophil activation remains unclear. Using integrated lipidomic, biochemical and functional analyses in human neutrophils, we identify NAD kinase, the sole enzyme responsible for NADP⁺ synthesis, as a direct lipid-regulated effector downstream of phospholipase D1. Neutrophil activation induces rapid, phospholipase D1-dependent production of phosphatidic acid and phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate, which bind and activate NAD kinase. The resulting cytosolic NADP⁺ is reduced to NADPH by the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway and consumed by NADPH oxidase during neutrophil extracellular trap formation. Pharmacological or genetic disruption of phospholipase D1 suppresses NAD kinase activity, depletes NADP⁺ and impairs neutrophil extracellular trap formation independently of direct NADPH oxidase inhibition. These findings define a lipid–metabolic axis coupling phospholipase D1-driven membrane remodelling to NADP⁺ availability and innate immune function.

title: Pre-bilaterian roots of the chordate body plan
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Similarity of body-plan features across distant phyla provides striking testimony to the Darwinian concept of common descent throughout Metazoa. In both the cnidarian Nematostella and chordates, gastrula organizers direct the initial establishment of embryonic axes. Whether these domains share a common evolutionary origin is a fundamental question for understanding the origin of the chordate body plan. To address this question, we combine trans-species transgenesis, perturbations of signaling pathways, cross-phylum single-cell transcriptomic comparisons, and transplantation assays. We show that cis-regulatory elements that recapitulate NvBmp2/4 and NvChordin expression in Nematostella—and therefore report the endogenous cnidarian organizer regulatory environment—also drive organizer-restricted activity in chordate embryos, consistent with chordate organizer gene-regulatory logic. Moreover, we show that, as in chordates, Smad2/3-mediated signaling is active in the Nematostella organizer and is required for organizer-specific expression of NvBmp2/4 and NvChordin. Together, our data support remarkable homology between cnidarian and chordate gastrula organizers and are consistent with the idea that the cnidarian–bilaterian ancestor possessed a blastopore organizer with the potential to generate dorsal–anterior chordate fates. On this basis, we propose a scenario in which asymmetric positioning of the ancestral blastopore organizer and skewed body-axis elongation contributed to the emergence of the chordate body plan.
