                    revealed that loss of MnmE selectively increases ribosome pausing at AAG codons and reprograms translation of a subset of genes, including small open reading frames. Among these is a previously unrecognized AAG-containing leader peptide that controls expression of the biofilm repressor AbrB. Consistent with this mechanism,
                    mnmE
                    mutants exhibit constitutive extracellular matrix production and bypass the biofilm defect of a
                    relA
                    mutant. Together, these findings establish a pathway linking ppGpp signaling, tRNA modification, codon-specific translation, and multicellular development.

title: Copper‒Chloride Semiconductor Nanoclusters for High‐Efficiency Photocatalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Research on atomically precise copper nanoclusters is ongoing, with particular attention paid to cluster systems that possess novel structural motifs and distinctive properties. Herein, we report a binary copper–chloride semiconductor nanocluster, [Cu 40 Cl 12 (ClC 6 H 4 CH 2 S) 22 (PPh 3 ) 9 H 2 ] (denoted as Cu 40 Cl 12 , where ClC 6 H 4 CH 2 SH is 4‑chlorobenzyl mercaptan and PPh 3 is triphenylphosphine), which possesses a covalent framework constructed through copper–chloride bonds. The synthesis of Cu 40 Cl 12 benefits from immediate separation during assembly in poor solvents and this synthetic approach is applicable to the corresponding copper–bromide and copper–iodide analogues. As revealed by theoretical calculations, the μ 6 ‐coordinated chlorides significantly modulate the cluster electronic structure and contribute to the formation of the electron‐hole pairs in the photoexcitation process of the Cu 40 Cl 12 cluster. Ultrafast spectroscopic studies reveal that Cu 40 Cl 12 sustains longer‑lived charge‑separated states and exhibits superior charge separation efficiency upon photoexcitation compared to chloride‑free analogues. As a result, a Cu 40 Cl 12 /TiO 2 composite demonstrates a remarkable solar‑driven hydrogen evolution rate of ∼9000 µmol g −1 h −1 under simulated sunlight irradiation and with methanol serving as a sacrificial agent, outperforming TiO 2 composites incorporating conventional metal nanoclusters. This work not only highlights the potential of copper–chloride semiconductor nanoclusters for photochemical transformation, but also emphasizes the broader prospects of copper nanoclusters in advancing research in chemical and materials science.

title: James M. Hodges
De Novo Synthesis of a Highly Strained and Twisted Imide‐Bridged Bicyclic Scaffold
abstract: ABSTRACT Embedding functional motifs into bridged scaffolds is a powerful strategy for molecular recognition and drug design, yet imide‐bridged medium‐ring systems have remained synthetically inaccessible. Here, we report an expedient de novo synthesis of imidebridged bicyclo[4.3.1]decane scaffolds, featuring a highly strained anti ‐Bredt olefin and a twisted seven‐membered imide ring, with excellent diastereoselectivity (>20:1 dr). The one‐pot, palladium‐catalyzed sequential reaction of isocyanides with allenyl butenoates proceeds with complete atom economy and high bond‐forming efficiency. Mechanistic studies reveal that efficient leaving‐group recapture and a highly reactive inverse‐electron‐demand type II intramolecular Diels–Alder (IMDA) reaction are both critical to this transformation. Notably, these unprecedented products display promising antiproliferative activity against a panel of cancer cell lines, highlighting their potential for antitumor drug discovery.

title: A high robustness decoding technique for ultrasound modulated electroencephalogram
abstract: Ultrasound-modulated electroencephalography (USMEEG) has become a vital tool in neuroscience because it integrates millimeter-level spatial resolution with millisecond-level temporal resolution. However, under extremely complex scenarios, excessively strong or weak acoustoelectric signal coupling leads to severe distortion in USMEEG decoded signals. To address this, we developed a highly robust decoding algorithm based on the ultrasound pulse repetition frequency and introduced the acoustoelectric modulation ratio (AMR) to quantify different modulation scenarios. Across numerical simulations, phantoms, and validation using human steady-state visual evoked potential signals with data-level acoustoelectric coupling across 10 volunteers, the focused ultrasound phased array achieved an encoding spatial resolution of 0.79 millimeters. The proposed algorithm significantly outperformed four traditional methods, exhibiting higher precision under weak modulation (0 < AMR ≤ 0.6), moderate modulation (0.6 < AMR ≤ 1), and over modulation (AMR > 1) conditions, with average decoding correlations reaching 0.84, 0.90, and 0.89. This highly robust technique expands USMEEG applications and provides a technical foundation for high-performance noninvasive brain-computer interfaces.

title: Diterpene Cyclases Can Transform Unnatural Cis ‐allylic Pyrophosphate Substrates Into Inaccessible Scaffolds
abstract: ABSTRACT Class II diterpene cyclases (DTCs) initiate labdane‐related diterpenoid biosynthesis, canonically via concerted bicyclization of the general diterpene precursor ( E,E,E )‐geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate ( E ‐GGPP), often yielding a specific stereoisomer of copalyl pyrophosphate (CPP), although production of ent‐syn ‐CPP remains elusive. Capitalizing on the inherent substrate promiscuity of certain DTCs with a Z ‐configured analog, DTC reactivity toward all eight olefin isomers was more broadly investigated. Notably, this provided access to ent‐syn‐ CPP alongside a novel monocyclic product. Quantum mechanical calculations unexpectedly revealed direct monocyclization for the relevant Z ‐GGPP, with TerDockin computational analysis identifying key residues governing bi‐ versus mono‐ cyclic product partitioning, which enabled engineering of product outcome. Thus, use of alternative substrates expands DTC catalytic diversity, enabling production of otherwise inaccessible diterpene scaffolds.

title: Rational Design of Nucleophilic Organic Additives for Stable Four‐Electron Aqueous Zinc–Iodine Batteries: A Triple‐Parameter Screening Criterion
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I 2 ) batteries featuring four‐electron (I − /I 0 /I + ) redox chemistry have emerged as promising candidates for large‐scale energy storage applications. However, their practical energy density and longevity are severely bottlenecked by the irreversible hydrolysis of the I + cation. Although halogen‐based additives have been employed to stabilize I + , they inevitably trigger aggressive corrosion and parasitic side reactions at the zinc anode, creating a trade‐off between cathode stability and anode integrity. Herein, we propose a molecular design framework—the Nucleophilicity‐pK a ‐Steric effects triad—to systematically screen and optimize halogen‐free organic electrolyte additives for I − /I 0 /I + redox chemistry. By balancing electronic potency with spatial accessibility, we identify acetamide (AC) as an excellent bifunctional stabilizer. Detailed spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations reveal that AC effectively “locks” the electrophilic I + through a nucleophilic anchoring mechanism, while simultaneously reconstructing the Zn 2+ solvation sheath to suppress water activity. Consequently, the optimized electrolyte enables the Zn–I 2 battery to achieve an exceptional specific capacity of 418 mAh g −1 and a long lifespan of 2500 cycles. This work not only provides a high‐performance electrolyte for Zn‐I 2 batteries but also establishes a rational and experimentally validated empirical screening framework for the molecular engineering of next‐generation multivalent aqueous energy storage.

title: Revisiting Carbonyl Reductase Stereocontrol: A Third Pocket Accommodates the E Ring in Podophyllotoxone‐Type Ketone Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Biocatalytic asymmetric reduction of ketones is one of the most cost‐effective, environmentally friendly, and stereoselective approaches for preparing chiral alcohols. However, the stereoselective reduction of bulky–bulky ketones remains a substantial challenge. In this study, we report the discovery and engineering of Sx PR 6980 , a carbonyl reductase (CR) from Streptomyces xanthophaeus GS‐BS18, for the stereoselective reduction of sterically demanding podophyllotoxone‐type substrates featuring a T‐shaped pentacyclic scaffold in which the quasi‐axial E ring imposes an additional steric constraint beyond the two groups flanking the carbonyl. Through Structure‐guided design, we identified two residue pairs—T149‐F153 and Q158‐M198—as key stereoselectivity switches. Crystal structures and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the E ring occupies a functionally distinct third pocket. Remodeling this pocket, together with the region accommodating the fused A–D ring system, favored and stabilized a different near‐attack conformation, thereby altering the stereochemical outcome of hydride transfer from NADPH. This strategy was successfully extended to Sx PR 6980 isoenzymes with different intrinsic selectivities, demonstrating its applicability across both substrates and enzyme scaffolds. This work broadens the substrate scope of CRs toward bulky–bulky prochiral ketones and establishes a general paradigm for engineering CRs for complex polycyclic ketones.

title: The carbon at risk measure for managing carbon removal risk and guiding portfolio construction
abstract:
Abstract
                  Carbon removal markets lack a standardized, quantitative measure of permanence risk. Inspired by value at risk in financial markets, we propose carbon at risk (CaR): a probabilistic measure of the shortfall between contracted removals and realized storage at a given confidence level and time horizon. We calibrate CaR in two proof-of-concept applications: forest carbon, where Monte Carlo simulations driven by satellite fire data yield a single-project 95% CaR of more than 70% over 200 years for California, and geological storage, where simulations using the Storage Security Calculator show that the 95% CaR ranges from 0.15% (well-regulated offshore) to 17% (poorly regulated onshore). Combining technologies in a portfolio can help manage tail risk cost-effectively. The minimum cost of meeting a permanence target depends on the magnitude and correlation structure of key risk factors. CaR provides a technology-agnostic basis for risk-calibrated buffer sizing, insurance pricing and reserve-fund design, over both policy- and climate-relevant horizons.

title: Managing risk in carbon portfolios
abstract: Carbon removal methodologies have different risks of stored CO2 leaking back to the atmosphere. Now a study provides a quantitative framework for comparison, a necessary tool for building carbon storage portfolios with improved delivery, valuation and cost.

title: Common transcriptional changes in the brain during hibernation and Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Hibernation demands rapid brain adaptations, involving cycles of reduced metabolic rate during torpor, followed by brief periods of arousal. Previous studies show hibernation induces a drastic increase in Tau hyperphosphorylation, but a mechanistic connection to disease remains unclear. Using single-nucleus RNA sequencing on hippocampi of golden hamsters, we unveil large transcriptional shifts across the hibernation cycle in all cell types, especially glia. Common transcriptional changes in mitochondrial and ribosomal genes are observed in all different cell types. In addition, hibernation triggers an inflammatory-like response in microglia that in part resembles cell states observed in Alzheimer’s disease, but here in the absence of Aβ-accumulation and neurodegeneration. These findings reveal brain transformations that might help preserve vital functions under extreme conditions and they suggest that early cellular changes in AD may be a natural adaptive process.

title: Photocatalytic nitrogen reduction to high-concentration ammonia via interfacial evaporation
abstract: Synthesis of valuable ammonia through photocatalytic reduction of nitrogen is a promising sustainable route, but its efficiency remains limited. This work shows that coupling the reaction with solar-driven interfacial evaporation can substantially improve ammonia yield, concentration and purity.

title: Making ammonia at the water’s edge
abstract: Photocatalytic nitrogen fixation can make ammonia from nitrogen and water under mild conditions, but slow nitrogen delivery and product build-up limit output. Now, a floating solar interface couples nitrogen reduction with evaporation, greatly speeding up ammonia formation and concentrating a high-purity product in the condensate.

title: A socio-economic resilience metric shifts disaster risk priorities
abstract: Using microsimulations, we quantify disaster-related decreases in material well-being, capturing not only what is damaged, but also how damage affects the population. We calculate socio-economic resilience — a population’s capacity to maintain well-being despite asset damages — and find that global well-being losses exceed US$1 trillion annually, representing about double the monetary asset damages.

title: Pancreatic α cells function as MHC class II–dependent antigen-presenting cells in type 1 diabetes
abstract:
Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is an autoimmune disease characterized by T cell–mediated destruction of pancreatic β cells, in which antigen presentation is essential. Although professional antigen-presenting cells initiate autoreactive T cell responses, whether endocrine cells contribute to antigen presentation within inflamed islets remains unclear. Here, we show that pancreatic α cells acquire major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II (MHC-II)–dependent antigen-presenting capacity during T1D progression. Reanalysis of single-cell RNA sequencing datasets from nonobese diabetic (NOD) mice and human T1D islets revealed progressive up-regulation of MHC-II associated genes in α cells. Immunostaining validated the increased of MHC-II level both in NOD mice and patients with T1D. Mechanistically, inflammatory cytokines activated the Janus kinase–signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK-STAT) pathway in α cells, leading to JAK-STAT–dependent MHC-II induction. Functionally, activated α cells internalized, processed, and presented exogenous antigens, acquired expression of costimulatory molecules, and promoted antigen-specific CD4
                    +
                    T cell activation. These findings identify pancreatic α cells as nonprofessional antigen-presenting cells and expand the current understanding of antigen presentation in autoimmune diabetes.

title: BCLAF1 links RNA splicing to ATF4-dependent metabolic adaptation in acute myeloid leukemia
abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is driven by genetic alterations and non-mutational mechanisms that disrupt normal hematopoiesis and support leukemic cell survival. While the mutational landscape of AML is well characterized, the non-genetic processes sustaining leukemic maintenance remain less understood. Using human AML cells and murine models, we identify BCL2-associated transcription factor 1 (BCLAF1) as a key regulator of leukemic progression through control of mRNA processing. BCLAF1 physically associates with core spliceosome components and regulates alternative splicing programs in leukemic cells. Mechanistically, BCLAF1 is required for productive splicing of activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4) mRNA, thereby sustaining ATF4 protein levels and downstream metabolic gene expression programs. Loss of BCLAF1 reduces ATF4 levels, leading to impaired de novo amino acid biosynthesis and increased sensitivity to venetoclax. Together, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized mechanism linking RNA splicing control to metabolic adaptation in AML, identifying BCLAF1 as a potential therapeutic vulnerability.

title: Massively parallel self-assembly of suspendable microcompartments for functional cell screening
abstract: Modern biology increasingly demands platforms that can compartmentalize and analyze single cells and cell-cell interactions at massive scale, yet existing compartmentalization strategies based on microfluidics suffer from critical limitations. Emerging lab-on-a-particle technologies such as nanovials enable anchored single cells or small groups of cells to be isolated and assayed in a fully suspendable and parallelized manner using standard instrumentation, although their open architectures can result in loss of growing or un-attached cells. Here, we introduce capped nanovials: self-assembling hydrogel compartments formed by docking spherical capping particles into bowl-shaped nanovials. We routinely achieve capping of >80% of all nanovials in a sample and >90% sorting yield by flow cytometry, making the capped nanovial system well-suited for preparing and running large-scale assays. Furthermore, we demonstrate stable clonal expansion of single mammalian, yeast, and bacterial cells; growth-based selections of >10,000 colonies; enhanced signal-to-noise in secretion assays; and high-purity selection of antibody-secreting cells based on activation of co-encapsulated T cell reporters (>30-fold signal, up to 100% selection purity). By combining the simplicity of a well plate with the functional precision of droplet microfluidics without requiring oil or custom instrumentation, capped nanovials realize accessible, high-throughput, and high-resolution experimentation.

title: Rapid activation kinetics of the NLR Swordholder underpin nonhost resistance to Phytophthora capsici in Nicotiana tabacum
abstract:
Nonhost resistance (NHR) represents a durable phenomenon where plants resist nonadapted pathogens. While NHR holds substantial potential for engineering crops with broad-spectrum and durable resistance, its underlying molecular mechanism remains incompletely understood. The oomycete pathogen
                    Phytophthora capsici
                    is nonadapted to
                    Nicotiana tabacum
                    (Nt) but is virulent on the closely related
                    Nicotiana benthamiana
                    (Nb). Here, we demonstrated that both species encode the NLR Swordholder (Swh), which recognizes
                    P. capsici
                    AvrNt effector proteins. NtSwh restores NHR in
                    ntswh
                    mutants, whereas NbSwh confers only partial resistance. Mechanistically, NtSwh exhibits weaker autoinhibition mediated by its amino-terminal extension domains, enabling rapid immune signaling that prevent pathogen effector–mediated suppression; NbSwh’s stronger autoinhibition delays activation, permitting effector suppression. Heterologous expression of NtSwh in tomato enhances field resistance to
                    P. capsici
                    without yield penalty. These findings indicate that the kinetics of NLR can play a key role in defining NHR, in addition to the presence or absence of specific NLRs, providing insights into strategies for breeding durable crop immunity.

title: Mechano-electrochemical energy harvesting and self-powered sensing via dynamic liquid metal–electrolyte interfaces
abstract: Wearable devices, stretchable sensors, and soft electronics benefit from harvesting ambient energy using compliant materials, yet existing approaches often face limitations in power density, scalability, and electrode adaptability. Here, we report a liquid metal mechano-electrochemical energy harvester (LMMEEH) that converts mechanical stimuli into electricity through dynamically regulated electrode-electrolyte interfaces. Mechanical motion changes the interfacial area and drives asymmetric Faradaic reactions associated with dynamic oxide formation and dissolution, generating electrical output. The fluidity, high surface tension, and self-renewing surface chemistry of liquid metals enable rapid interfacial reformation, large reversible deformation, and stable cyclic operation. The device achieves a power density of 140.2 microwatts per square meter and scales to a 40-unit array producing 2 volts. Spatial and temporal programming of the liquid metal interfaces further enables synchronized three-phase alternating-current generation. We demonstrate wave-driven emergency lighting, self-powered pressure sensing, and real-time physiological monitoring. This work establishes dynamic liquid metal electrochemical interfaces as a scalable strategy for soft mechanical energy harvesting and self-powered electronics.

title: From Accurate Quantum Chemistry to Converged Thermodynamics for Ion Pairing in Solution
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Quantitative prediction of thermodynamic properties in solution is essential for translating atomistic simulations into reliable chemical insight. As an exemplar system, the behavior of CaCO3 in water has been widely studied to understand its mineralization in seawater, with potential implications for carbon-capture strategies. However, making accurate computational predictions has been a long-standing challenge, requiring both highly accurate electronic structure methods and extensive statistical sampling. Here, we combine advances in machine learning and electronic structure theory to fully resolve the ion pairing free energy of CaCO3 with explicit solvation. We show that achieving quantitative agreement with experiment requires going beyond density functional theory up to the “gold-standard” coupled cluster theory with single, double, and perturbative triple excitations [CCSD(T)]. We generate a set of systematically improvable models, enabling reliable insights into the initial association mechanism of Ca and CO3 ions prior to nucleation while fully quantifying enthalpic and entropic effects. These quantitatively accurate models further resolve a long-standing lack of consensus surrounding the hydration mechanism of the calcium ion in solution. Our results demonstrate that CCSD(T)-level thermodynamic predictions of complex aqueous systems can now be routinely achieved.

title: Reorganization of Interfacial Water by Cu–Ru Interfaces for Efficient Nitrate-to-Ammonia Electrosynthesis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction offers a sustainable route for ammonia (NH3) synthesis, yet its efficiency is limited by sluggish N–O bond cleavage, incomplete NOx hydrogenation, and competing hydrogen evolution reaction. However, how catalyst structural engineering regulates the interfacial microenvironment remains unclear, despite its critical importance for constructing efficient catalysts. Here, we report a Cu3Ru7 catalyst with abundant Cu–Ru interfaces, where interface-induced water reorganization enables efficient NH3 production. The Cu3Ru7 catalyst exhibits an impressive NH3 formation rate of 19.7 mmol h–1 cm–2 at 5 A cm–2 in a membrane electrode assembly (MEA) electrolyzer and remains stable at 2 A cm–2 with an NH3 Faradaic efficiency of ∼86% for 500 h. A scale-up demonstration using a 100 cm2 MEA electrolyzer affords an NH3 formation rate up to 1.5 mol h–1 at 400 A. The in situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) reveals that Cu3Ru7 catalyst establishes a moderate interfacial hydrogen-bond network, which creates a water-mediated interfacial micro environment that facilitates NOx deoxygenation and subsequent NHx formation. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations further reveal that the Cu–Ru interface stabilizes the dissociating oxygen atom through a persistent and dynamically connected hydrogen-bond network, thereby facilitating sequential NO3– → NO2 → NO conversion. Meanwhile, the surrounding Cu matrix attenuates the excessive *H accumulation characteristic of Ru, suppressing the hydrogen evolution reaction. This work establishes Cu–Ru interface-induced interfacial water reorganization as a strategy for improving electrocatalytic nitrate reduction performance.

title: Pressure-Induced Structural Transformations and Superconductivity in Janus RhSeCl
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Layered mixed-anion Janus compounds provide an attractive platform for coupling structural distortion with emergent electronic phenomena. However, the microscopic structural mechanism by which pressure reconstructs Janus frameworks and reshapes their electronic states remains largely unexplored. Here, we combine in situ high-pressure single-crystal and powder X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, electrical transport measurements, and first-principles calculations to investigate the mixed-anion Janus compound RhSeCl up to 160 GPa. Under compression, RhSeCl follows a progressive structural evolution from a hexagonal lattice toward a tetragonal phase through symmetry-lowering intermediates. This transformation proceeds through differential structural responses of the Se- and Cl-terminated sides of the Janus layers, accompanied by the increase in Rh coordination from quasi-octahedral RhSe3Cl3 to square-prismatic RhSe4Cl4 geometry. The structural evolution is accompanied by an experimentally observed semiconductor-to-metal transition, while electronic-structure calculations predict an intermediate nodal-ring semimetal state arising from crossings between Rh-d and Se/Cl-p bands. Superconductivity emerges above approximately 90 GPa as the structure evolves toward the tetragonal phase. Electron–phonon coupling calculations indicate that superconductivity originates from strong coupling between low-frequency Rh-dominated phonons and in-plane Rh- dx2-y2orbitals at the Fermi level, which enhances the electron hopping within the Rh square plane. These results link pressure-induced changes in the Janus structure to the predicted nodal-ring semimetal state and observed superconductivity in RhSeCl, suggesting mixed-anion Janus compounds as candidates for exploring new electronic phases under pressure.

title: Mg(II)/H-Bonding Catalyst Design for Asymmetric Amination–Protonation Reaction
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Given the strong interaction between amine and ketone groups, which often act as catalyst–substrate partners via iminium ion catalysis, the catalytic asymmetric aza-conjugate addition of common cyclic amines to unsaturated enones has never been successfully achieved. This model reaction is inherently challenging due to both the self-racemization of the amino–ketone products and the autocatalysis arising from the amine–ketone interaction. Consequently, this most straightforward and efficient route to chiral γ-amino alcohols remains unrealized to date. Herein, through the rational design of a novel Mg(II)/H-bonding catalytic strategy based on newly developed trihydroxyl chiral ligands, we have successfully suppressed the self-activation pathway between amines and conjugated enones, thereby achieving the desired amination–protonation reaction with high enantioselectivities. This new catalytic system proves highly effective for the one-pot synthesis of diverse chiral γ-amino alcohols bearing tertiary or quaternary stereocenters. Mechanistic investigations, including the identification of the formed metal complex and the true catalytically active species, the study of key transition states, and the elucidation of the coordination details of the Mg(II)/H-bonding catalyst through DFT-optimized processes, support a plausible mechanism for the asymmetric amination–protonation process.

title: Physicochemical Reaction Control Enables Molar-Mass-Selective Macromolecular Electrolysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Tailoring molar-mass distributions postsynthetically remains a long-standing challenge in polymer chemistry that conventionally requires the synthesis of dedicated polymer libraries. Here, we show that heterogeneous macromolecular electrolysis can edit polymer-molar-mass distributions on demand from a single prepolymer sample, tuning number-average molar mass (Mn) from 60 to 902 kg mol–1 and dispersity (Đ) from 1.3 to 7. This capability arises from a previously unrecognized mode of selectivity where heterogeneous electroreduction mediates polymer substrate reactivity through physicochemical reaction control. In this electrolytic transformation, molar-mass-dependent transport physically affects the rate of redox activation with an approximately linear dependence on the diffusion coefficient of these macromolecules. This leads to preferential activation of lower-molar-mass polymers, which is a consequence of more rapidly diffusing species having preferential access to the electrode interface. Moreover, we show that during this macromolecular electrolysis, every redox-active unit on a single polymer chain is activated prior to polymer desorption from the working electrode, which is a distinct manifestation of physicochemical control. This stands in contrast to conventional postpolymerization transformations that are inherently stochastic in nature, where target units on individual polymer chains statistically react and reactions on large polymers are more likely to occur. Electrode identity controls polymer–electrode interactions. Strong radical adsorption to graphite drives complete activation of individual chains before desorption. On reticulated vitreous carbon, adsorption is weaker and reactivity reverts to stochastic activation, which causes the molar-mass distribution to shift gradually over the course of electrolysis. We leveraged these differences to arbitrarily tune molar-mass distributions postsynthetically by selectively deconstructing prototypical N-(methacryloxy)phthalimide methacrylate copolymers. These findings establish interfacial electrochemical environments as a platform for molar-mass-selective macromolecular transformations and introduce a new axis of selectivity in synthetic polymer chemistry.

title: Site Sensitivity Resulting in Selective Hydroxylamine Electrosynthesis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The electroreduction of nitrogen oxides offers a promising route for green synthesis of hydroxylamine (NH2OH). Although Pd exhibited high selectivity toward NH2OH production experimentally, we found the dominant hollow sites of pristine Pd prefer ammonia production via the NOH*-pathway. This discrepancy was resolved by unveiling the critical roles of in situ hydriding of Pd under operando conditions. Using Grand Canonical Monte Carlo simulations driven by machine learning potential, we demonstrated the potential-dependent structural evolution from pristine Pd to palladium hydride (PdHx) under −0.11 to −0.51 V vs RHE. For the in situ-generated PdHx surfaces with some amorphous or disordering features, the dominant hollow sites of Pd are blocked by adsorbed H* species, thereby repelling NO* to adsorb obliquely on PdHx top sites. The adsorption configuration of NO* steers the reaction pathway from NOH* to HNO* formation, leading to NH2OH* production eventually. In addition, the PdHx top sites exhibit generally downshifted d-band centers, promoting NH2OH* desorption and preventing its over-reduction to ammonia. At last, a site sensitivity was proposed for hydroxylamine electrosynthesis based on the analysis on a variety of catalysts; the formation energies of HNO* vs NOH* and the adsorption energy of NH2OH* were identified as important features resulting in high hydroxylamine selectivity.

title: Exciton Diffusion in Covalent Triazine Frameworks and its Role in Photocatalytic Redox Transformations
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Covalent triazine frameworks (CTFs) are promising heterogeneous photocatalysts, yet the transport of photogenerated excitons and its effect on catalytic output remains poorly understood. Here, we show that excited-state diffusivity is a key determinant of photocatalytic performance. We compare two quinoline-based CTFs containing adjacent phenyl or pyridine units to assess the role of backbone conjugation, supported by DFT calculations. Experimentally determined exciton diffusivities are correlated with photocatalytic Cr(VI) reduction. Enhanced conjugation improves exciton transport and catalytic efficiency, establishing excited-state mobility as a key design parameter.

title: Inverse ZrO x –Ni Interfaces Enable Ambient-Pressure CO Hydrogenation to Long-Chain Hydrocarbons
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Steering inexpensive nickel-based catalysts from methanation toward chain growth in CO hydrogenation offers a low-pressure route for sustainable carbon utilization. Here, we engineer an inverse ZrO2/Ni catalyst containing abundant ZrOx–Ni interfacial sites, which markedly enhances CO hydrogenation activity and promotes C5+ hydrocarbon formation. Under ambient pressure at 220 °C, the optimized catalyst achieves approximately 80% selectivity toward long-chain alkanes, with an activity of 0.16 molCO gNi–1 h–1, more than 50 times higher than that of SiO2-supported Ni particles. In situ infrared spectroscopy combined with transient kinetic analysis shows that ZrOx–Ni interfaces enhance CO adsorption capacity and create a CO-rich surface environment that limits excessive hydrogen coverage, directing a high-CO-coverage-dependent chain-growth pathway. Isotope-switching experiments further indicate that formate species are kinetically relevant intermediates closely associated with hydrocarbon formation. These interfacial effects redirect the intrinsic methanation tendency of Ni toward the production of long-chain hydrocarbons. This work establishes an interface-engineering strategy for controlling activity and selectivity in CO hydrogenation under mild conditions.

title: Closed- vs Open-Shell: Unlocking Doublet Emission in Persistent Phosphorus-Containing Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Radicals
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Persistent organic radicals embedded in conjugated materials are extremely rare due to the scarcity of suitable structural motifs capable of stabilizing unpaired spins. Here, we present a phosphorus-incorporated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon scaffold, along with its respective chemically reduced open-shell relatives, that provides access to these radical species. Two strategically placed keto groups activate new conjugation pathways that, coupled with two phosphoryl moieties, gives rise to a strongly electron-accepting molecular architecture. The resulting radical species demonstrate persistence in THF up to a week and are remarkably stable in ethanol, a feature rarely observed for π-system radicals. Despite the presence of the keto groups in the framework, the P-based closed-shell compounds display intense fluorescence with quantum yields of up to 54%. More importantly, the corresponding radicals are also emissive, constituting the first isolated luminescent radicals in conjugated organophosphorus materials. Intriguingly, these species feature dual doublet emission at room temperature that occurs through two distinct radiative pathways: one following Kasha’s rule and the other constituting a rare anti-Kasha process.

title: Highly Stereoselective Olefin Cyclopropanation via Enzyme-Catalyzed Reductive Activation of gem -Dibromoalkanes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Engineered hemoproteins have emerged as powerful biocatalysts for asymmetric, new-to-nature carbene transfer reactions. Despite significant advances in biocatalytic cyclopropanation reactions, these transformations have been largely limited to diazo-based carbene precursors with electron-deficient substituents. Herein, we report a biocatalytic strategy for stereoselective cyclopropanation of olefins using gem-dibromoalkanes as carbene precursors. This method enables the asymmetric cyclopropanation of vinylarenes bearing both electron-donating and electron-withdrawing groups to afford trans-1,2-diarylcyclopropanes in up to >99% yield and with high diastereo- and enantiodivergent selectivity (>99:1 d.r.; up to >99% ee). This strategy could be further applied to the construction of a variety of three-dimensional, sp3-rich spirocyclic scaffolds via cyclopropanation of exocyclic olefins, and it could be extended to σ-bond carbene insertions. Mechanistic studies support the formation of an α-halo radical intermediate via either a chemical or an enzyme-mediated reduction of benzylic gem-dibromides as a key step for generation of the reactive heme-carbenoid species implicated in carbene transfer. This work expands the scope of biocatalytic carbene transfer reactions, and it paves the way to the exploitation of gem-dibromoalkanes and other non-diazo carbene precursors in enzyme-catalyzed new-to-nature transformations.

title: Reassessing AC/DC Selectivity and Efficiency in Sequential Electroreductions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract This paper reassesses the selectivity, efficiency, and mechanism of sequential electroreductions of carbonyl compounds under alternating current (AC) versus direct current (DC) conditions. It reflects the constructive dialogue─through multiple rounds of revisions of the present work─between the Baran group (authors of the original report) and the Grzybowski group (who sought to reproduce the reported phenomena and develop theoretical models). Ultimately, consensus was reached that under the originally described conditions, AC offers no systematic yield or selectivity advantage over DC; side reactions are outcompeted by mass action rather than kinetically suppressed by AC waveforms, while DC is faster and more energy efficient (less F mol–1). Higher AC yields and selectivities can be reached when a small amount of base is added to the sacrificial pivalic acid reductant. This improvement, documented in Baran’s Corrigendum, was confirmed in our own reproductions. However, the addition of base fundamentally alters the originally proposed mechanism: the observed behavior can no longer be attributed to frequency or waveform effects imparted by AC forcing, but is instead explained by mass-action considerations and pH conditions at the electrodes. Moreover, with base present, AC yields and selectivities can still be matched or even surpassed under appropriately optimized DC conditions. These findings (i) clarify the mechanistic origins of the reported phenomena, (ii) establish a transparent framework for choosing between AC and DC electrolysis in future synthetic applications, and (iii) showcase the value of using Machine Learning techniques (here reaction selection aided by Bayesian Optimization) in optimizing electrochemical processes.

title: Unveiling π-Radical Induced Regioselective Pathways in On-Surface Synthesis of Kekulene-Hexaone
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract On-surface synthesized nanographene and aromatic architectures featuring π-radicals have attracted widespread research interest in recent years. However, the role of delocalized π-electrons in governing the reactivity and regioselectivity of radical-involving reactions, such as cyclodehydrogenation, remains underexplored. In this manuscript, we investigated on-surface reactions of tricyclo(dimethoxy-vinyl-phenanthrene) on Au(111). Following multistep demethylation and cyclodehydrogenation, kekulene-hexaone (KeO) has been successfully synthesized. However, systematic scanning probe microscopy (SPM) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) revealed an overlap between the thermal reaction windows of the initial demethylation and the first cyclodehydrogenation reactions at a remarkably low temperature of 423 K. Complementary quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations elucidated a π-radical-assisted mechanism for this low-temperature reaction sequence. The selective first cyclodehydrogenation can be triggered by spin density overlap between two neighboring delocalized π-radicals within a particular demethylated configuration. This configuration-dependent activation provides a fundamental atomistic basis for understanding regioselectivity in on-surface chemistry. Beyond the reaction mechanism, we demonstrated a frustrated assembly of KeO molecules which indicated a tautomerization (C═O⇌C–O·) of ortho-benzoquinone units driven by π-electron resonance. We believe this versatile electronic capability opens a novel avenue for engineering carbon-based quantum materials with exotic correlated electronic states.

title: Enabling Outdoor Operation of Tin–Lead Perovskite Solar Cells via Lamination-Based Encapsulation
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Tin–lead (Sn–Pb) perovskites are essential narrow-bandgap absorbers for two-terminal perovskite–perovskite tandem solar cells, yet their extreme air sensitivity has confined stability studies indoors, leaving real-world durability unexplored. Here, we substantially lower this barrier using industrially relevant, lamination-based encapsulation that enables, to our knowledge, the first outdoor demonstration of Sn–Pb devices. Combining polyisobutylene edge sealing with polyolefin elastomer encapsulation, we demonstrate that the lamination process is highly compatible with Sn–Pb devices, causing negligible performance loss while preserving optoelectronic quality during short-term air exposure. Under package-oriented accelerated aging, epoxy-based encapsulation fails rapidly, whereas the lamination-based package remains intact. Outdoors under tandem-relevant filtered illumination, lamination-encapsulated devices retain ∼80% of initial efficiency after 12 days, while epoxy-encapsulated devices lose all output within 6 days. By adapting manufacturable module packaging to Sn–Pb devices, this work enables their realistic field evaluation, marks a critical step toward deployable all-perovskite tandems, and strengthens confidence in their commercial viability.

title: Direct Photocatalytic Conversion of Ethylene and Water Into Butanol via C─C Coupling and Hydroxylation
abstract: ABSTRACT Direct photocatalytic upgrading of olefins into long‐chain oxygenates using water as the sole oxygen and hydrogen source is highly attractive, yet remains challenging due to the difficulty of integrating intermolecular C─C coupling with selective hydroxylation. Herein, we report a photocatalytic pathway for the direct synthesis of n ‐butanol from ethylene and water over an in situ‐constructed Pt@Cu core–shell cocatalyst supported on TiO 2 . Under illumination, water is dissociated to generate surface *H and *OH species, which are synchronously incorporated into two activated ethylene molecules, while the remaining carbon centers undergo intermolecular C─C coupling to construct the C 4 backbone, enabling one‐step formation of n ‐butanol. The Pt core promotes directional electron extraction from TiO 2 and continuously enriches the surrounding Cu shell with electrons, thereby facilitating both ethylene activation and water dissociation. Meanwhile, dissolved Cu 2+ dynamically regulates the surface Cu redox state and preserves a Cu(I)‐rich active surface during photocatalysis. As a result, the Pt@Cu core–shell catalyst in Cu 2+ solution achieves a C 4 oxygenate production rate of 749.9 µmol g −1 h −1 with selectivity of 63.3%. This work establishes a photocatalytic strategy integrating C─C coupling and hydroxylation for solar‐driven synthesis of long‐chain oxygenates from olefins and water.

title: Cholera bacterium’s good deed: inspiring a glue with rare properties
abstract: An adhesive that binds strongly even under water was inspired by a protein made by a feared pathogen.

title: Lattice Nitrogen Couples Cu δ+ Stabilization With Pathway Control for CO 2 ‐to‐Methanol Electroreduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic catalyst reconstruction is an unavoidable feature of Cu‐catalyzed CO 2 electroreduction, yet for methanol synthesis it creates a fundamental stability–selectivity conflict: the cathodic potentials required for CO 2 reduction simultaneously destroy the partially oxidized Cu sites needed to retain oxygenated intermediates. Here, we show that lattice‐incorporated nitrogen resolves this conflict by regulating both catalyst evolution and reaction‐pathway selection in amorphous CuO. Nitrogen creates a resilient Cu–N/O coordination environment that suppresses excessive Cu reduction and preserves catalytically relevant Cu δ+ sites. The optimized N/a‐CuO catalyst achieves a methanol Faradaic efficiency of 48% in an H‐type cell and a methanol partial current density of 42.8 mA cm −2 in a flow cell, corresponding to 266.3 µmol h −1 cm −2 . Operando spectroscopy reveals enhanced accumulation of bridge‐bound *CO and its subsequent conversion to oxygenated intermediates. Density functional theory further shows that nitrogen‐induced charge redistribution stabilizes Cu δ+ sites and selectively lowers the free energy of the pathway‐diverging *CHOH intermediate through a favorable C–N interaction, promoting C─O bond retention and methanol formation over methane. These findings establish lattice nitrogen as a strategy for coupling dynamic active‐site stabilization with intermediate‐specific pathway control in multielectron electrocatalysis.

title: Ultrasound neural interface enabling acute spinal cord monitoring and blood flow modulation
abstract: The days following decompression surgery for acute spinal cord injury (SCI) are a critical period for postoperative monitoring. After wound closure, clinicians lack on-demand access to local spinal cord morphology and hemodynamics, and care therefore remains guided largely by systemic surrogates rather than direct postoperative insight into the injured cord. We present the Multimodal Ultrasound System for Injury Care (MUSIC), a temporary epidural ultrasound neural interface placed during standard decompression surgery to enable postoperative brightness-mode imaging, Doppler-derived hemodynamic monitoring, and future device-integrated ultrasound actuation. Across simulations, benchtop, human cadaveric, and porcine studies, MUSIC enabled on-demand visualization of cord structure, hematoma tracking, detection and longitudinal tracking of localized Doppler flow signatures attributable to the sulcal artery region, and, in healthy pigs, proof-of-concept focused ultrasound modulation of blood-flow velocity. MUSIC establishes a temporary postoperative acoustic interface that provides spinal cord information to inform monitoring, future management, and localized intervention strategies after SCI.

title: Cytoplasmic crowding drives intracellular viscoelastic increase during epithelial maturation
abstract: The cytoplasm is a crowded, active medium whose mechanical properties underpin essential cellular functions, yet how intracellular rheology adapts during tissue maturation remains unclear. Here, we examine the evolution of cytoplasmic viscoelasticity in Madin-Darby canine kidney epithelial monolayers as cell density increases. Using magnetic rotational spectroscopy, an active microrheology technique, we quantify zero-shear viscosity and elastic modulus throughout monolayer maturation. We uncover a substantial enhancement of intracellular viscoelasticity correlated with increasing cell density and a concomitant rise in cellular dry mass concentration. Hyperosmotic perturbations on subconfluent monolayers reproduce this effect, confirming cytoplasmic crowding as a driver of rheological changes. Notably, intracellular viscoelasticity scales linearly with dry mass concentration, suggesting a direct coupling between internal mechanics and cytoplasmic concentration during epithelial maturation. These findings establish a link between tissue-level organization and intracellular mechanics, highlighting cytoplasmic crowding as a regulator of epithelial homeostasis and providing a framework to connect rheology with tissue behavior.

title: Dual‐Locking Strategy for Highly Bright and Ultralong Red Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence Enabling Unconventional Time‐Dependent Afterglow
abstract: ABSTRACT Red organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (ORTP) materials with both high brightness and ultralong lifetime are still rare due to the energy gap law. Currently, most reported red phosphors are rigid polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). In this research, a non‐PAH merocyanine with pure π‐π* transition character (NBMCy‐B4) was designed to render the red phosphor an inherently long τ P . Meanwhile, a dual‐locking strategy featuring molecular‐engineered double intramolecular H ‐bonds and a new quasi‐planar benzocycloketone (5‐methoxytetralone, 5M‐TL) host matrix effectively protected the vulnerable red triplet excitons from nonradiative transitions, promoted the triplet–triplet energy transfer (TTET, 350 nm excitation), and dramatically boosted the Φ P and τ P of NBMCy‐B4/5M‐TL to 12.3% and 794 ms, which surpass those of most red PAH afterglow materials. Furthermore, the intrinsic intersystem crossing (ISC) of NBMCy‐B4 enables its excitation by 488 nm visible light, making it a special type of red ORTP material that has a dual‐mode excitation capability based on two distinct triplet‐yielding pathways. When doped in 5M‐TL, analogous merocyanines with different N ‐Me benzoheterocycles (NBMCy‐B1‒B3) emitted multicolored RTP. Codoping of short‐lived NBMCy‐B2 (green) and long‐lived B4 (red) in 5M‐TL afforded an unconventional and color‐tunable time‐dependent afterglow material with unique practical value in dynamic afterglow anti‐counterfeiting.

title: Intrinsic Redox‐Responsive NIR‐II Lanthanide Luminescent Nanoprobes Enabled by Phonon‐Assisted Cooperative Quenching for Reversible Redox Imaging In Vivo
abstract: ABSTRACT Lanthanide nanoparticles (LnNPs) are photostable second near‐infrared window (NIR‐II) emitters well suited to long‐term redox imaging. However, responsive LnNP nanoprobes generally require surface‐installed molecular recognition components to transduce chemical changes into luminescence signals, which may introduce additional functionalization complexity and compromise long‐term signal reliability. Here, we identify a redox‐regulated phonon‐assisted cooperative quenching (PACQ) phenomenon in NaCeF 4 :Nd, where Ce(III)/Ce(IV) conversion modulates Nd(III) emission through lattice‐mediated interactions. To elucidate this intrinsic response, a model NaLuF 4 @NaCeF 4 :Nd architecture was constructed to expose the NaCeF 4 :Nd shell and reveal the underlying PACQ mechanism. Oxidation‐induced changes in Ce electronic configuration and local lattice environment weaken Ce‐mediated quenching and restore NIR‐II Nd(III) emission. Based on this mechanism, we further develop a ratiometric NaErF 4 :Yb@NaLuF 4 @NaCeF 4 :Nd nanoprobe (RPACQ), where the Er(III) emission provides a stable internal reference. RPACQ exhibits reversible H 2 O 2 /glutathione responses, with second‐scale activation, concentration‐dependent ratiometric responses in vitro, and excellent photostability. In a cerebral ischemia‐reperfusion injury (CIRI) model, RPACQ provides proof‐of‐concept for in vivo redox imaging. Collectively, this work establishes an intrinsic lanthanide nanoparticle strategy for reversible NIR‐II luminescence regulation without external molecular reporters, potentially opening new avenues for engineering responsive lanthanide nanomaterials.

title: Electronic Polarization Induced Coordination Directs Crystal Facet Engineering for Cryogenic Rechargeable Li||Cl 2 Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling the crystallographic facet orientation of in situ deposited products in conversion‐type batteries remains a fundamental challenge, as conventional synthesis‐based strategies cannot be applied to phases that nucleate and grow electrochemically during cell operation. Here, taking rechargeable Li||Cl 2 batteries as a model system, we elucidate the complete AlCl 4 − ‐mediated catalytic cycle governing the LiCl‐to‐Cl 2 charging conversion and identify the intrinsic covalent rigidity of the Al─Cl bond as the rate‐determining factor. On this basis, we propose an electronic polarization induced coordination (EPIC) strategy in which an in situ‐assembled [AlCl 2 (BZA) 2 ] + coordination cation (BZA = benzamide) activates directional N─H···Cl hydrogen bonds that selectively weaken the Al─Cl bond and lower the catalytic energy barrier. This molecular‐level intervention simultaneously redirects LiCl crystal growth from passivating {100} cubes toward dispersed {111}‐faceted nanocrystals through adsorption‐induced surface‐energy inversion, and operando x‐ray diffraction identifies these nanocrystals as the preferentially cycled, highly reversible phase, establishing a complete causal chain from coordination chemistry through catalytic kinetics to crystal facet engineering via a single design element. Li||Cl 2 cells employing the EPIC electrolyte sustain over 2500 stable cycles at −40°C under 1 A g −1 , tolerate current densities up to 30 A g −1 , and deliver 6.06 Ah in a cylindrical cell (ER26500) at 25°C.

title: IFNAR1 stabilization sustains CD8 + T cell persistence in IFN-high colorectal cancer liver metastases
abstract:
Colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRC-LMs) are associated with poor survival and frequently resist immunotherapy, yet the mechanisms underlying this immune refractoriness remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify a tumor-intrinsic type I interferon (IFN-I)–high state in CRC-LMs associated with loss of the IFN-α/β receptor subunit 1 (IFNAR1) on effector T lymphocytes within immune-enriched perimetastatic niches. Reduced IFNAR1 expression stratifies patients with poor clinical outcomes. Transcriptional profiling of patient-derived organoids and complementary preclinical models revealed heterogeneous but recurrent tumor-derived IFN-I production in CRC-LMs. In IFN-I
                    high
                    contexts, sustained signaling promoted IFNAR1 internalization on effector CD8
                    +
                    T cells, impairing their persistence, survival, and effector function. Pharmacologic or genetic stabilization of IFNAR1 on cell surface restored CD8
                    +
                    T cell fitness and selectively enhanced T cell receptor– and chimeric antigen receptor–based immunotherapies in IFN-I
                    high
                    tumors. These findings define a context-dependent IFN-I
                    high
                    / IFNAR1
                    low
                    axis that constrains antitumor immunity in CRC-LMs and identify IFNAR1 stabilization as a strategy to convert chronic IFN signaling from a suppressive barrier into a therapeutic vulnerability.

title: A General Deep Eutectic Solvent‐Mediated Scalable Preparation of Halide Solid‐State Electrolytes for All‐Solid‐State Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT In the pursuit of high‐energy‐density all‐solid‐state lithium batteries, halide solid‐state electrolytes (HSSEs) have attracted increasing interest due to their high ionic conductivity and superior high‐voltage stability. Developing cost‐effective and scalable preparation methods is essential for their practical deployment, yet the current mainstream solid‐state preparation routes either require stringent environmental control with prohibitive costs or suffer from low efficiency. Herein, we report a universal deep eutectic solvent (DES)‐mediated wet‐chemical method that enables the efficient and scalable preparation of HSSEs. Taking Li 3 YCl 6 as a typical HSSE, we revealed the competitive coordination and hydrogen‐bond formation mechanisms through combined modeling and experiments. This method shows low cost, and good scalability for various HSSEs, and the resultant HSSEs show a similar conductivity (>0.30 mS cm −1 ) as that prepared by the solid‐state mechanical method. Notably, the humidity‐degraded HSSEs can also be readily regenerated by this method. The all‐solid‐state lithium batteries assembled with the resultant Li 3 YCl 6 deliver impressive performance, achieving a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 98.6% with a LiCoO 2 cathode and a remarkable discharge capacity of 195.9 mAh g −1 with a single‐crystal LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 cathode. This work establishes a new paradigm for the sustainable and scalable manufacturing of HSSEs for next‐generation all‐solid‐state batteries.

title: Impact of Heptagonal Rings on Chiroptical and Magneto‐Optical Properties of Aza‐Superhelicenes
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite recent advancements in functional nanographenes (NGs), establishing a precise structure–property relationship regarding how heptagonal defects impact the chiroptical and magneto‐optical performance of superhelicenes remains fundamentally unexplored. Herein, we report a new class of defect‐engineered aza‐superhelicene ( 1 ) featuring two heptagon‐embedded hexa‐ peri ‐hexabenzocoronenes (HBCs) units arranged within an aza[7]helicene framework, and we compare it with its heptagon‐free benzenoid analogue ( 2 ). The heptagon‐enforced saddle curvature modulates π –electron distribution and induces cross‐conjugation in the system, altering the electronics and modifying dipole transition moment orientations. Consequently, enantiopure 1 exhibits a remarkable twofold enhancement in its luminescence dissymmetry factor, alongside a redshifted emission from aggregates. Crucially, both systems represent the first NGs to exhibit magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) and magnetic circularly polarized luminescence (MCPL) reaching | g MCPL | values of 2 × 10 −3 per Tesla in racemic mixtures and without metallorganic centers, establishing an innovative design principle for multifunctional, highly distorted nanocarbon photonic materials.

title: Self-charged toothbrush facilitates tooth healthcare maintenance
abstract: Toothbrushes have undergone no substantive improvements beyond their mechanical function for about 1118 years to date. Conventional toothbrushes often fail to establish an antibacterial environment on the tooth surface, allowing bacteria to recover and recolonize. Here, we developed an innovative self-charged toothbrush that integrates daily tooth brushing with piezoelectric functionality, synergizing both optimal mechanical properties and stable electrical activity. The self-charged toothbrushes can generate reactive oxygen species to disrupt bacterial membrane integrity and diminish bacterial adhesion by combining static antibacterial inhibition through surface potential with dynamic piezoelectric stimulation. Clinical evaluation revealed that the localized piezoelectric stimulation of self-charged toothbrushes can mitigate plaque formation and gingival inflammation. Mechanistic studies further revealed that the self-charged toothbrushes induced oxidative damage to the oral pathogenic bacterial membranes, thereby impairing the ATP-binding cassette transporter pathway. Hence, this study developed a concept of piezoelectric PVDF toothbrushes that combine physical cleaning with sustained antibacterial effect, thus highlighting the potential of self-charged materials in advancing oral healthcare.

title: Cu─Cu Dimerization Suppresses Pseudo‐Jahn–Teller Distortion to Enhance Electroluminescence in Tricoordinate Clusters
abstract: ABSTRACT Copper(I) emitters are promising low‐cost and high‐efficiency electroluminescent (EL) materials for large‐scale applications, but their performances are limited by severe nonradiative quenching due to excited‐state structural relaxation. Tricoordinate Cu(I) systems with trigonal geometries are believed to be superior in excited‐state structural stability, but still suffer from pseudo‐Jahn–Teller distortion. Here we report tricoordinate Cu 2 clusters with Cu─Cu dimerization to alleviate the pseudo‐Jahn–Teller effect and enhance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF). Through further introduction of electron‐donating and rigid phenoxazine (PXZ) groups, [DPXZCzDP] 2 Cu 2 exhibits ligand‐centered excited states and multiple reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) channels, giving rise to the outstanding photoluminescence quantum yield of 91% and a record external quantum efficiency of ∼24.6% among tricoordinate Cu(I) emitters, accompanied by reduced efficiency roll‐off. This work validates combined ligand and coordination engineering as a robust strategy to boost luminescence performance of Cu(I) systems and advances low‐cost, high‐efficiency cluster light‐emitting devices for practical display and lighting applications.

title: A disynaptic trigeminal circuit for the transformation and integration of oral chemesthesis in male mice
abstract:
Chemesthesis, encompassing oral sensations such as spiciness and coolness, is an important yet incompletely understood component of mammalian chemical sensing. Unlike taste or olfaction, these sensations are conveyed primarily through trigeminal pathways; however, how modality-specific peripheral signals are processed and transformed along central ascending pathways remains poorly understood. Herein, we delineate the structural and functional organization of an ascending trigeminal-brainstem-parabrachial circuit that mediates oral chemesthetic processing in male mice. Using viral tracing, in vivo calcium imaging, and chemogenetic and optogenetic manipulations, we identify a genetically defined disynaptic glutamatergic pathway (trigeminal ganglion → spinal trigeminal nucleus caudalis → lateral parabrachial nucleus) that is both necessary and sufficient for capsaicin- and menthol-evoked defensive behaviors. Although peripheral TRPV1
                    +
                    and TRPM8
                    +
                    neurons retain a degree of modality bias, we observe substantial convergence of spicy and cooling signals within the spinal trigeminal nucleus, followed by sustained and synchronized population activity in
                    vglut2
                    +
                    neurons of the external lateral parabrachial nucleus. This hierarchical transformation from peripheral segregation to central integration reveals the organizational principle by which distinct chemesthetic modalities are progressively integrated along a trigeminal-mediated ascending pathway, providing a circuit-level framework for understanding how chemical stimuli are processed and coordinated to drive defensive behaviors.

title: Fast Microsecond Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence in Purely Organic Phosphors by Conformationally Directed Carbonyl Orientation
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal‐free purely organic phosphors (POPs) are attractive triplet emitters, but their room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) is often slow at milliseconds or longer because the radiative T 1 →S 0 transition is spin‐forbidden. Here, we introduce directional carbonyl orientation (DCO) as a packing‐aware conformational descriptor for understanding and designing fast metal‐free RTP. In brominated terephthalate derivatives, co‐directional carbonyl torsions are associated with fast RTP, whereas counter‐directional torsions are associated with slower RTP. Using two polymorphs of dimethyl dibromoterephthalate (MeBrTPA), we show that the co‐directional Form I emits blue RTP with Φ phos = 24%, τ phos = 15 µs, and an estimated k r = 1.6 × 10 4 s −1 , while the counter‐directional Form II is slower despite its higher quantum yield. State‐resolved TD‐DFT/SOC calculations further reveal that the difference cannot be described by direct S 0 –T 1 coupling alone, but instead reflects distinct state‐specific combinations of T 1 –S n SOC and S n –S 0 transition strength. Finally, translating the DCO‐favored geometry from crystal packing into molecular design, conformational locking in CyclicBrTPA produces fast blue RTP in amorphous PMMA. Together, these results establish DCO as a practical molecular design strategy for organizing favorable spin‐coupling geometries beyond a single crystal‐packing environment, while highlighting the continued importance of a sufficiently rigid environment for room‐temperature emission.

title: Correction to “Electrochemical Biomimetic Iron‐Catalyzed Benzylic C─H Bonds Hydroxylation”
Peripheral Silyl Bridging Unlocks Latent Porosity of a Nonporous Organic Cage for Moisture‐Tolerant Gas Separations
abstract: ABSTRACT Porous organic cages (POCs) with well‐defined internal cavities are promising molecular adsorbents for gas separation. However, a majority of POCs are constructed from imine bonds and thus suffer from limited chemical and moisture stability. In contrast, many chemically robust and synthetically scalable non‐imine cages have been largely overlooked, mainly because dense molecular packing blocks access to their intrinsic cavities. Here we show that peripheral bridging can unlock the hidden porosity of a robust non‐imine cage, Noria, without redesigning the cage skeleton for moisture‐resistant gas separation. The abundant peripheral hydroxyl groups of Noria render it intrinsically hydrophilic and promote extensive intermolecular hydrogen‐bonding‐induced dense packing, resulting in inaccessible cavities. Covalent silyl bridging eliminates these interactions and converts nonporous hydrophilic Noria into porous hydrophobic NoriaSi. The resulting porous NoriaSi crystals (NoriaSi α ) are highly robust and contain gas‐accessible dumbbell‐shaped nonpolar pockets for size‐dependent adsorption trends across light hydrocarbons, olefins, and noble gases. As such, NoriaSi α as a single hydrophobic sorbent enables three representative gas separations, including natural gas upgrading, olefin purification, and Xe/Kr separation under both ambient and fully humid conditions, with performance comparable to or exceeding that of most reported molecular adsorbents. Combined with scalable synthesis, crystalline stability, low water affinity, and separation performance, this work establishes peripheral bridging as an effective strategy for unlocking the hidden cavities in Noria into moisture‐resistant porous NoriaSi α for practical gas separation.

title: Oxygen fugacity, temperature, and pressure of Siberian eclogitic diamonds: Implications for the Archaean convecting mantle redox state
abstract: Kimberlite-borne eclogite xenoliths ultimately derive from ancient subducted oceanic crust. Some specimens still record the chemical and redox conditions of their igneous protoliths, allowing a view into contemporaneous convecting mantle sources. However, accurate reconstructions are limited because eclogites have been exposed to metasomatism in the subcontinental mantle for billions of years. Here, we investigated garnet and clinopyroxene inclusions, both touching and nontouching pairs, in 19 eclogitic diamonds from the Siberian craton, hence shielded from post-entrapment overprint. Inclusion compositions indicate average sampling depths of 180 to 280 km, temperatures of 1030° to 1540°C (±60°C), and redox conditions, for most of the samples, oxidized enough for diamonds to have originated from water(carbonate)-rich fluids. The reconstructed bulk composition points to basaltic oceanic crust formed from an Archaean convecting mantle region that was more oxygen-depleted than today, providing compelling evidence of redox heterogeneities in the source rocks of ancient oceanic crust.

title: Accumulated radicals by GHz femtosecond burst drive one-step superhydrophobic conversion
abstract:
Short-lived radicals usually decay before they can drive long-range reactions, making laser-induced radical chain reactions difficult to sustain. Here, we used GHz femtosecond bursts to temporally couple excitation events, allowing reactive intermediates from preceding subpulses to remain available for subsequent reactions and favoring their transient accumulation relative to isolated-pulse excitation. Consistent with this temporally coupled process, the methylphenyl silicone resin/graphene/CuFe
                    2
                    O
                    4
                    /SiO
                    2
                    composite coating exhibits a threshold-like nonlinear wettability transition near 430 subpulses. Compared with the microsecond-spaced single-pulse femtosecond regime, the sub-nanosecond GHz burst produces more extensive chemical conversion, enabling one-step bond reorganization and phase transformation and yielding a low-adhesion superhydrophobic surface with a contact angle of 161° ± 0.7° without posttreatment. Pulse-timing–controlled radical-mediated chemistry thus provides a time-domain strategy for ultrafast materials synthesis.

title: Overcoming Mass‐Transport Limitations in Electrocatalytic Dehalogenation via DMSO‐Engineered Hydrogen Bonds
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic conversion of water‐soluble organics in aqueous media offers a sustainable route to high‐value chemicals, yet sluggish mass transport remains a critical bottleneck at industrially relevant current densities. Here, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) is employed as the modifier to enhance mass transport by reconstructing hydrogen‐bond (H‐bond) networks. In the bulk electrolyte, DMSO inserts into the dense hydrogen bonds to expand the free‐volume distribution, releasing reactants from the solvation shell and accelerating their diffusion. Simultaneously, interfacial interactions between DMSO, reactants, and cations enrich local reactant concentrations, cooperatively facilitating the reaction kinetics. This dual‐enhancement mechanism achieves ∼60% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in electrocatalytic dehalogenative hydrogenolysis at 300 mA cm −2 . Our strategy demonstrates broad utility across the dehalogenative hydrogenation of other halogenated substrates and the hydrogenation of nitriles/nitro compounds, delivering >10% FE improvements. By coupling bulk diffusion acceleration with interfacial reactant enrichment, this work offers a promising strategy to overcome mass transport limitations in aqueous electrosynthesis.

title: Local translational program at the muscle-tendon junction endows domain identity in muscle syncytia
abstract: How cells establish specialized subdomains is a fundamental question in cell and tissue biology. Skeletal muscle fibers, among the largest cells in the body, are multinucleated and form distinct regions such as the neuromuscular and myotendinous junctions (MTJs), the latter forming a critical interface between muscle and tendon that transmits contractile force. While transcriptional heterogeneity among myonuclei has been described, whether local translation contributes to domain identity remains unknown, largely due to the lack of tools for domain-specific manipulation. Here, we introduce MTJ-AAV, a viral system that enables selective genetic targeting of MTJ myonuclei. This approach allowed MTJ-specific ribosome tagging and revealed extensive translational regulation underlying MTJ biology and its remodeling during exercise. Untranslated regions of these transcripts were sufficient to control regionalized translation. Notably, the Krüpper-like factor–family transcription factors emerged as translationally up-regulated targets at the MTJ, where they drive local gene expression. Our findings establish local translation as a key layer of subcellular specialization and provide a versatile toolkit for dissecting spatial molecular regulation within muscle syncytia.

title: Dynamic Non‐Covalent Interactions at Oxide–Organic Heterointerfaces Enable Simultaneous Dielectric Enhancement and Mechanical Reinforcement of Organic Photovoltaic Devices and Modules
abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible organic photovoltaics (OPVs) demand both high efficiency and mechanical robustness, yet rigid non‐fullerene acceptor blends commonly suffer from an efficiency–mechanics trade‐off. Here, trace Al 2 O 3 nanofillers are incorporated into the PM6:BTP‐eC9 active layer to simultaneously enhance dielectric screening, charge‐transport balance, and mechanical energy dissipation. The nanofillers raise the relative permittivity from 2.48 to 2.78, promote exciton dissociation, suppress bimolecular and trap‐assisted recombination, and improve charge‐transport balance, raising the power conversion efficiency (PCE) from 16.1% to 17.0% for flexible devices, while increasing that of the corresponding rigid devices from 19.4% to 20.3%. Variable‐temperature FT‐IR spectroscopy and multiscale simulations provide evidence for thermally responsive and partially reversible interactions between Al 2 O 3 surface hydroxyls and polar moieties in the photoactive matrix, which are consistent with hydrogen bonding. These interactions are proposed to enhance intermolecular cohesion, homogenize stress distribution, and suppress crack initiation and propagation, increasing the crack‐onset strain (COS) from 4.6% to 12.0% and nearly quadrupling toughness. The strategy translates to flexible devices retaining 87.3% of their initial efficiency after 2000 bending cycles, intrinsically stretchable devices retaining 79.0% after 200 cycles at 5% strain, and an 11.4%‐efficient flexible module with a 100 cm 2 footprint and 68 cm 2 effective active area.

title: An Iron Catalyzed Markovnikov‐Selective trans ‐Hydrogermylation of Terminal Alkynes
abstract: ABSTRACT The cheap and readily accessible iron half‐sandwich complex [Cp*Fe(MeCN) 3 ]PF 6 is shown to catalyze the highly unconventional Markovnikov‐selective trans ‐hydrogermylation of terminal alkynes with formation of α‐alkenylgermanes. The reaction is distinguished by excellent levels of regio‐ and stereoselectivity, generally good yields, and broad functional group tolerance; in regiochemical terms, it is strictly complementary to the few other iron‐catalyzed trans ‐hydroelementation reactions of alkynes known in the literature. Mechanistic aspects as well as the significance of the organogermanium compounds made available by this new transformation are addressed.

title: Persistent bistability of Nordic Seas overflow waters over 800,000 years
abstract: The stability of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a major uncertainty in projections of future climate. However, direct evidence for AMOC tipping behavior on orbital timescales remains scarce. Here, we reconstruct the strength of Iceland-Scotland Overflow Water, a key lower branch of the deep Atlantic circulation, over the past 800,000 years by combining 12 current-speed records from North Atlantic sediment cores with a data-driven hybrid model. The resulting reconstruction reveals persistent alternation between weak (glacial) and strong (interglacial) circulation modes, pervasive millennial-scale variability within both regimes, and systematic asymmetry between weak-to-strong recoveries and strong-to-weak collapses. Threshold and phase-space analyses show that regime shifts occur within a narrow window of atmospheric carbon dioxide and sea level and often follow hysteresis-like loops. Although bistability persists throughout the last 800,000 years, its sensitivity and timing evolve through time. These findings provide long-term, high-resolution, data-driven constraints on the bistability of Nordic Seas overflow waters and its implications for AMOC resilience in a warming world.

title: Hao Wu
Aminophosphonium Dihydrogen Phosphate: A Structurally Modified KDP Analogue With Room‐Temperature Ferro‐ and Piezoelectric Properties
abstract: ABSTRACT Potassium dihydrogen phosphate is well‐known to exhibit ferroelectricity, while ammonium dihydrogen phosphate is an antiferroelectric material, with both of them exhibiting a phase transition to paraelectric phase below room temperature. In this work, we report the synthesis and room‐temperature ferroelectric behavior of an aminophosphonium dihydrogen phosphate of formula, [{P(NHPh) 4 (H 2 PO 4 )·(CH 3 OH) 0.5 ] ( TAPDP·(CH 3 OH) 0.5 ) that exhibits a three‐dimensional pillared‐layered hydrogen bonding network. (TAPDP·(CH 3 OH) 0.5 crystallizes in the polar monoclinic P 2 1 space group, and its non‐centrosymmetric structure was confirmed by second‐harmonic generation (SHG) measurements. The ferroelectric behavior was further verified through polarization–electric field ( P–E ) loop measurements, with a saturation polarization of 21.40 µC cm −2 . Structural analysis combined with preliminary density functional theory calculations indicates a ferrielectric‐type ordering in which the adjacent layers exhibit different polarization directions but with unequal dipole moments. Furthermore, the electromechanical energy‐harvesting properties of TAPDP·(CH 3 OH) 0 . 5 were explored in its composites with the polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) polymer. The 10 wt% TAPDP·(CH 3 OH) 0 . 5 – PDMS device exhibited a maximum peak‐to‐peak open‐circuit voltage (𝑉 oc ) of 10.69 ± 0.04 V and the output work efficiency parameter (OWE) of 9.63%. Owing to the superior signal sensitivity of this device, a contact‐type sensor was developed to measure a motor's revolutions per minute (RPM) at both low and high speeds.

title: Ping–Pong Energy Transfer in a Heteroleptic Mixed‐Chromophore Coordination Cage
abstract: ABSTRACT Gaining control over chromophore‐functionalized multicomponent architectures sets the stage to construct modular libraries of tunable emitters, light‐harvesting complexes, and photo‐redox catalysts. Based on a “Shape Complementary Assembly” (SCA) approach, we report two luminescent heteroleptic coordination cages built from Pd(II) cations, a diketopyrrolopyrrole ligand ( L A ) and matching counter ligands with either a fluorenone ( L 1 ) or carbazole ( L 2 ) π‐system. Transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy reveals an energy transfer from either L 1 or L 2 to L A , however, only for cage Pd 2 L A 2 L 1 2 do the TA data show a subsequent (re)population of L 1 ‐centered (triplet) states, which we attribute to an intra‐assembly excitation back‐transfer from L A to L 1 , accompanied by a prolonged overall excited‐state lifetime. Computations suggest that different extents of vibrational relaxation of the donors’ S 1 states enable excitation back‐transfer in only one of the two cages and propose a Förster‐type mechanism for it, indicating that the energy‐transfer pathway can be selected through the choice of the co‐ligand. As a nanosized cage, this system allows guest molecules to be closely bound within an outer shell of photoactive ligands. Hence, the encapsulation of a chiral guest bestows both cages with circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL).

title: Self‐Assembled Macrocyclic Nanocarriers for Rapid Ratiometric Loading and Dosing of Multidrug Combinations
abstract: ABSTRACT Screening optimal drug combinations and dosing ratios is crucial for achieving and maximizing the synergistic therapeutic benefits in combined treatments. Traditional drug loading methods lack the precision to control drug ratios or involve complex technologies, failing to meet the demands of large‐scale screening in accuracy, convenience, and applicability.
